output_spec: The result is a source database with one row per source, rating its completeness, accuracy and corroboration. It ends with a statement of what is known and what is unknown, and names the items that rest on single-source support.

technique: **CRAAP test (currency, relevance, authority, accuracy, purpose)**
what_it_does: Screens a single source against five criteria. Artefact: a checklist judgement; read authority, accuracy and purpose first for vendor material.
fit_test: It is used to judge a specific claim, because it examines the page, not the claim's wider support. The URL domain heuristic is weak (note author's judgement).
status_and_evidence: **Documented.** A library handout with criteria and questions; its creator is not named on it. ([Meriam Library CRAAP test handout](https://library.csuchico.edu/sites/default/files/craap-test.pdf))
purpose: Screens one source against five criteria (currency, relevance, authority, accuracy, purpose) and produces a checklist judgement for the evidence base.
use_when: Use when you need a quick check on whether a web page, report or vendor document is fit to cite.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The target is a specific claim and not the page, because the test does not examine the claim's wider support. A domain name used as a proxy for authority is weak.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE1-04 :: moving off the page tests the authority and purpose judged here; substitutes for :: HE-01 :: when document_genre is organisation report and only a short screen is needed
typical_model_failure: Infers authority from how professional the page looks, and invents author credentials not shown on the page.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:repeat runs; decision-informing:prompt variation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:repeat runs; high-stakes:prompt variation; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; language model; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the criteria are scored without a rule, when authority cannot be checked outside the page, or when purpose is hidden (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a checklist with one row per criterion (currency, relevance, authority, accuracy, purpose), each giving a judgement and the reason for it. It ends with an overall judgement of the single source, with the authority, accuracy and purpose rows stated first when the source is vendor material.

technique: **SIFT (stop, investigate the source, find better coverage, trace claims to the original; claim verification and fact-checking)**
what_it_does: Moves a reader off the page to find who published a claim, what others say, and where it began. Artefact: a short judgement and a located original context; read whether the original differs from the version met.
fit_test: The claim is technical and the checker cannot judge the expertise involved.
status_and_evidence: **Practice.** Created by Caulfield, who has taught the moves since 2017; the page gives no effectiveness data and says a brief check is often enough for casual reading. ([Caulfield, SIFT: the four moves](https://hapgood.us/2019/06/19/sift-the-four-moves/))
purpose: Moves from a claim to its publisher, to other coverage and to the original source, and produces a short credibility judgement with the original context located.
use_when: Use when you meet a claim online and need to know who is behind it, what others say and where it began.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The claim is technical and the checker cannot judge the expertise involved.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE1-05 :: lateral reading is the step that investigates the publisher; pairs with :: TC-04 :: SIFT finds the original and claim verification checks the claim against its text
typical_model_failure: Reports a trace to an original that it did not find, or accepts the first search result as independent coverage.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:repeat runs; decision-informing:prompt variation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:repeat runs; high-stakes:prompt variation; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; language model; source selection
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the original cannot be found, when coverage found is derived from one origin, or when search results are limited (reporting bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a short judgement of the claim's source that names who published it, what other sources say about it, and where the claim began. It states the located original context and says whether the original differs from the version first met.

technique: **Lateral reading**
what_it_does: Leaves the page quickly and opens other sources to learn about the publisher before reading in depth. Artefact: a judgement of publisher credibility.
fit_test: No independent coverage of the publisher exists.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** A 2017 Stanford study of fact checkers, historians and students was reported in the Stanford Daily, but the full text and effect sizes were not opened.
purpose: Leaves the page to read about the publisher in other sources and produces a judgement of publisher credibility.
use_when: Use when you need to decide whether to trust a publisher you do not know before reading its content in depth.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: No independent coverage of the publisher exists.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE1-04 :: lateral reading is one move within the wider source and claim trace
typical_model_failure: Treats search results written by the publisher or its allies as independent coverage.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:repeat runs; decision-informing:prompt variation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:repeat runs; high-stakes:prompt variation; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; language model; source selection
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the only coverage found is from the publisher, or when coverage is sparse (imprecision and reporting bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a judgement of the publisher's credibility based on what other sources say about the publisher. It names the sources consulted and states the finding drawn from each before giving the overall judgement.

technique: **Triangulation (source, method, investigator and theory triangulation; corroboration)**
what_it_does: Compares independent lines of evidence on one question. Artefact: a convergence table; read agreement, disagreement and the reasons.
fit_test: The sources copy each other, which looks like corroboration but is one source.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** The general technique (Denzin 1970) was recalled and not opened. The independence requirement appears in the Admiralty definition of the best credibility grade. ([Wikipedia, Admiralty code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiralty_code))
purpose: Compares independent lines of evidence on one question and produces a convergence table of agreement, disagreement and reasons.
use_when: Use when two or more independent sources or methods address the same question and you need to know whether they agree.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_rules: source_dependence=copied or derived :: sources that copy each other count as one source
not_for_text: The sources share an origin, so agreement looks like corroboration but is one source repeated.
related_techniques: should follow :: HE1-01 :: grade each source before comparing lines of evidence; should follow :: IS-06 :: test source dependence before counting agreement
typical_model_failure: Counts agreement between sources that cite each other as independent corroboration.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; source selection; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when sources share an upstream origin or method, or when disagreement is explained away without evidence (inconsistency and risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a convergence table with one row per line of evidence and columns for what each line shows on the question. It states where the lines agree, where they disagree, and the reason given for each disagreement.

technique: **Evidence hierarchies and certainty grading (study design levels, risk-of-bias assessment, Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation or GRADE)**
what_it_does: Ranks study designs and rates confidence in a body of evidence. Artefact: a level or a certainty rating from high to very low; read the reasons for downgrading, not only the label.
fit_test: The question has no randomised designs, as with policy descriptions.
status_and_evidence: **Documented.** Cochrane rapid review guidance has reviewers grade certainty of evidence; the five GRADE domains were not verified. ([Cochrane Rapid Reviews Methods Group guidance (2020)](https://methods.cochrane.org/sites/methods.cochrane.org.rapidreviews/files/uploads/cochrane_rr_-_guidance-23mar2020-final.pdf))
purpose: Ranks study designs and rates confidence in a body of evidence from high to very low, and produces a certainty rating with reasons for downgrading.
use_when: Use when you need to say how much confidence a body of studies deserves and why.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The question has no randomised designs, as with policy description, so a design hierarchy ranks everything low.
related_techniques: should follow :: HE-02 :: risk of bias must be assessed for each study before certainty is rated; pairs with :: HE1-08 :: certainty grading is the final step of a systematic review
typical_model_failure: Applies a certainty label without the domain reasoning, or downgrades once for a study design and again for the same weakness.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement; source selection
certainty_limits: Certainty ratings are themselves judgements. Check that each downgrade names a domain (risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, reporting bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result gives, for the body of evidence, the study design level and a certainty rating from high to very low. It lists the reasons for any downgrading beside the rating, so the label is not given alone.

technique: **Systematic review**
what_it_does: Collects all eligible studies by a pre-specified, reproducible search, appraises and synthesises them. Artefact: a flow diagram, evidence table and synthesis; read exclusion reasons and the risk-of-bias table.
fit_test: The question is broad (mapping) or too few comparable studies exist.
status_and_evidence: **Documented.** The Cochrane Handbook treats finding unpublished studies as important for minimising bias and rates grey literature searching as highly desirable. ([Cochrane Handbook, chapter 4](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-04))
purpose: Collects all eligible studies by a pre-specified, reproducible search, appraises and synthesises them, and produces a screening log, an evidence table and a synthesis.
use_when: Use when you need the most complete and least biased answer the published evidence can give to a narrow question.
requires_minimum: at least two eligible studies; a written protocol with eligibility criteria; two independent reviewers
not_for_text: The question is broad, so a map would serve better, or too few comparable studies exist to synthesise.
related_techniques: should follow :: FQ-01 :: a structured question fixes the eligibility criteria; pairs with :: HE-02 :: each included study needs design-specific appraisal; pairs with :: HE1-10 :: a scoping review can narrow a broad question first
typical_model_failure: Reports a search as exhaustive without a protocol, invents studies, or leaves out exclusion reasons.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; source selection; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with an incomplete search, a single screener, unpublished studies missed (reporting bias) and heterogeneous studies (inconsistency).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a flow diagram of studies found, screened, excluded and included, an evidence table with one row per included study, and a synthesis. It includes the exclusion reasons and a risk-of-bias table with one row per study.

technique: **Rapid review**
what_it_does: A systematic review with steps streamlined to meet a deadline of about one week to six months. Artefact: a narrative synthesis; read which shortcuts were taken, because they define the risk of missed studies.
fit_test: A missed study could change the conclusion.
status_and_evidence: **Documented.** Cochrane guidance recommends dual screening of at least 20 per cent of abstracts, English-language searching and limited grey literature; its recommendations are provisional and based mainly on a survey of 20 Cochrane entities. ([Cochrane Rapid Reviews Methods Group guidance (2020)](https://methods.cochrane.org/sites/methods.cochrane.org.rapidreviews/files/uploads/cochrane_rr_-_guidance-23mar2020-final.pdf))
purpose: Runs a systematic review with streamlined steps to meet a deadline and produces a narrative synthesis that states the shortcuts taken.
use_when: Use when a review is needed within about a week to six months and the cost of a missed study is moderate.
requires_minimum: at least two eligible studies; dual screening of at least 20 per cent of abstracts
not_for_rules: stakes_tier=high-stakes :: a missed study could change a high-stakes conclusion
not_for_text: A missed study could change the conclusion even at lower stakes.
related_techniques: substitutes for :: HE1-08 :: when stakes_tier is decision-informing or exploratory and a deadline applies; pairs with :: HE-02 :: included studies still need appraisal
typical_model_failure: Presents the output as a full systematic review and does not list which steps were cut.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; source selection; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with every shortcut: limited databases, English only, little grey literature (reporting bias) and single screening.
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a narrative synthesis of the included studies that comes with a list of the shortcuts taken in the review. It states for each shortcut the risk of missed studies that it creates.

technique: **Scoping review (evidence mapping)**
what_it_does: Maps the extent, types and gaps of evidence on a broad topic without judging the strength of findings. Artefact: a charted table; read the gaps.
fit_test: A decision needs an effect estimate.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** Only chapter headings were seen; the body text did not load, and the claim that appraisal is often omitted is general knowledge.
purpose: Maps the extent, types and gaps of evidence on a broad topic without judging the strength of findings, and produces a charted table.
use_when: Use when you need to know what evidence exists on a broad topic and where the gaps are before choosing a narrower question.
requires_minimum: a broad question, inclusion criteria and a charting form
not_for_rules: claim_level_needed=estimate an intervention effect|explain mechanism or counterfactual :: a scoping review does not judge strength of findings
not_for_text: A decision needs an effect estimate.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE1-08 :: the map identifies a narrow question that a systematic review can then answer; should follow :: FQ-01 :: the review question and inclusion criteria come from framing
typical_model_failure: Judges the strength of findings while charting, or presents a gap in its own search as a gap in the literature.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; source selection; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with a narrow search, one charter, and inclusion criteria applied loosely (reporting bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a charted table with one row per included source and columns for the type, extent and focus of the evidence. It ends with a list of the gaps in the evidence and does not judge the strength of the findings.

technique: **Meta-analysis**
what_it_does: Combines effect estimates from separate studies into a weighted average with a confidence interval. Artefact: a forest plot, pooled effect and heterogeneity statistics; read heterogeneity before the pooled number.
fit_test: Studies differ too much, or are few and small. Funnel plot guidance was not read.
status_and_evidence: **Documented.** The Handbook warns that results can mislead if bias, variation and reporting bias are ignored, that the heterogeneity test has low power with few studies, and that common methods are biased for rare events. ([Cochrane Handbook, chapter 10](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-10))
purpose: Combines effect estimates from separate studies into a weighted average with a confidence interval and produces a forest plot, a pooled effect and heterogeneity statistics.
use_when: Use when several similar studies report comparable effect estimates and you need one pooled estimate with its uncertainty.
requires_minimum: at least two studies with effect estimates and standard errors, or the counts or means needed to compute them
not_for_text: Studies differ too much in design or population, or are few and small.
related_techniques: should follow :: HE1-08 :: pooled studies should come from a reproducible search; should follow :: HE-02 :: study bias must be appraised before pooling; substitutes for :: HE1-12 :: when content_type is tabular and comparable effect estimates are available
typical_model_failure: Computes the pooled estimate by hand with arithmetic errors, or reports the pooled number without reading heterogeneity.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:sensitivity analysis; decision-informing:code execution for arithmetic; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:code execution for arithmetic; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:provenance log
error_sources: input data; statistical assumptions; source selection
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with heterogeneity (inconsistency), small studies and publication bias (reporting bias), and biased included studies (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a forest plot with one row per study, a pooled effect with its confidence interval, and heterogeneity statistics. The heterogeneity is stated before the pooled number.

technique: **Narrative, thematic and qualitative evidence synthesis (including meta-ethnography)**
what_it_does: Combines findings across studies in words or themes when pooling numbers is not appropriate. Artefact: a structured narrative or theme set; read how themes link back to studies.
fit_test: It becomes an unstructured summary.
status_and_evidence: **Documented.** Cochrane guidance says to synthesise narratively unless studies are similar; named qualitative techniques (Thomas and Harden 2008; Noblit and Hare) were recalled and not opened. ([Cochrane Rapid Reviews Methods Group guidance (2020)](https://methods.cochrane.org/sites/methods.cochrane.org.rapidreviews/files/uploads/cochrane_rr_-_guidance-23mar2020-final.pdf))
purpose: Combines findings across studies in words or themes when pooling numbers is not appropriate, and produces a structured narrative or theme set linked back to studies.
use_when: Use when studies are too different to pool and you still need to say what they find together.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The synthesis becomes an unstructured summary with no link from each theme back to the studies.
related_techniques: should follow :: HE1-08 :: synthesised studies should come from a reproducible search; substitutes for :: HE1-11 :: when content_type is text and effect estimates are not comparable
typical_model_failure: Writes a fluent summary that blends studies together and loses which study supports which theme.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when themes do not trace to studies, when study quality is unappraised (risk of bias), and when findings conflict (inconsistency).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a structured narrative or a set of themes, with each theme described in words and linked back to the studies that support it. It states the findings across studies without pooling numbers.

technique: **Reflexive thematic analysis (Braun and Clarke)**
what_it_does: Identifies and interprets patterns of meaning across qualitative data. Artefact: themes with data extracts, in six phases from familiarisation to writing up.
fit_test: Themes are only topic headings, or counts are presented as findings.
status_and_evidence: **Documented.** The authors separate coding-reliability techniques from their reflexive technique, in which coding is treated as subjective. ([Braun and Clarke, thematic analysis chapter (UWE repository)](https://uwe-repository.worktribe.com/output/6633690))
purpose: Identifies and interprets patterns of meaning across qualitative data in six phases and produces themes with supporting extracts.
use_when: Use when you need to understand what people mean across interviews, documents or posts and a person can read the whole set.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The themes are only topic headings, or counts of coded items are presented as findings.
related_techniques: conflicts with :: CK-01 :: coding in this method is treated as subjective, so agreement statistics do not apply
typical_model_failure: Proposes themes that name topics, and presents them as findings without the reflexive interpretation the method needs.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when themes are not tied to extracts, the analyst's position is not stated, or sampling is purposive and limited (indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a set of themes, each with a name, a description of the pattern of meaning it captures, and data extracts that support it. It ends with a written account that interprets the themes across the data.

technique: **Framework analysis (Framework Method)**
what_it_does: Sorts coded data into a case by theme matrix. Artefact: a matrix; read across rows for cases, down columns for themes, and look for empty cells.
fit_test: The data are heterogeneous, or the spreadsheet look tempts counting of responses. Documents may call for discourse or narrative analysis instead.
status_and_evidence: **Documented.** Seven stages are documented; it is time consuming and needs an experienced qualitative lead. ([Gale et al. (2013), the Framework Method, BMC Medical Research Methodology](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3848812/))
purpose: Sorts coded qualitative data into a case by theme matrix and produces the matrix for reading across cases and themes.
use_when: Use when you have many cases such as interviews and need to compare themes across them with a visible audit trail.
requires_minimum: similar topics across cases; an experienced qualitative lead
not_for_text: The data are heterogeneous, or the spreadsheet layout tempts counting of responses. Documents may call for discourse or narrative analysis instead.
produces: codebook:fixed; coded corpus:coded; comparison matrix:draft; result:draft
related_techniques: substitutes for :: HE1-13 :: when volume_class is readable by a person and comparison across cases is the aim
typical_model_failure: Fills matrix cells with summaries that drift from the data, and reports counts of cells as response frequencies.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with heterogeneous cases, a single coder, and summaries that no longer trace to the data.
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a matrix with one row per case and one column per theme, each cell holding a short summary of the coded data for that case and theme. It notes the empty cells and states what reading across the rows and down the columns shows.

technique: **Content analysis (conventional, directed and summative)**
what_it_does: Codes text into categories, then counts or interprets category use. Artefact: category frequencies or a category structure; read agreement between coders where used.
fit_test: Meaning depends on context that categories remove.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** No source was opened.
purpose: Codes text into categories, then counts or interprets category use, and produces category frequencies or a category structure.
use_when: Use when you need to say how often topics or categories appear in a body of text.
requires_minimum: a coding scheme
not_for_text: Meaning depends on context that the categories remove.
related_techniques: pairs with :: CK-01 :: agreement between coders tests whether the categories are applied consistently; substitutes for :: MM-08 :: when volume_class is readable by a person and manual coding is feasible
typical_model_failure: Applies categories inconsistently across documents and reports counts without any agreement check.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:repeat runs; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:repeat runs; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with low coder agreement, a corpus that was not sampled for the question (indirectness), and category drift.
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a category structure or a table of category frequencies, with one row per category and a count or interpretation of how often the category is used. It reports agreement between coders where more than one coder was used.

technique: **Discourse analysis (critical discourse analysis)**
what_it_does: Examines how language constructs topics and positions actors. Artefact: an interpretive account of framing, checked against quoted passages.
fit_test: The question is one of fact.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** Named as an alternative for some text data in the Framework Method paper ([Gale et al. (2013), the Framework Method, BMC Medical Research Methodology](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3848812/)); no primary source was opened.
purpose: Examines how language constructs topics and positions actors and produces an interpretive account of framing checked against quoted passages.
use_when: Use when the question is how something is framed or who is positioned how in speeches, policy documents or media.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_rules: insight_wanted=cause :: the technique interprets framing and does not trace cause
not_for_text: The question is one of fact, not of how language is used.
related_techniques: pairs with :: MM-11 :: reading a sample closely tests the frames that scaled framing analysis finds
typical_model_failure: Asserts framing effects without quoting the passages that show them, and treats interpretation as established fact.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when interpretations are not checked against quotations and when the texts sampled are unrepresentative of the discourse (indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is an interpretive account of how the language constructs the topic and positions the actors. Each claim in the account is checked against a quoted passage that is reproduced in the result.

technique: **Grounded theory coding (open, axial and selective coding; constant comparison)**
what_it_does: Builds categories and a theory from data through coding and constant comparison. Artefact: codes, memos and a theory.
fit_test: Ordinary coding is labelled grounded theory without iterative sampling.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** No source was opened.
purpose: Builds categories and a theory from data through open, axial and selective coding with constant comparison and produces codes, memos and a theory.
use_when: Use when no theory fits the topic and you need to build one from the data by coding and comparing as you collect.
requires_minimum: iterative sampling in the full technique
not_for_text: Ordinary coding is labelled grounded theory without iterative sampling or constant comparison.
produces: codebook:draft; coded corpus:coded; hypotheses matrix:draft; result:draft
related_techniques: substitutes for :: HE1-13 :: when volume_class is readable by a person and a new theory is the aim
typical_model_failure: Produces a tidy theory in one pass with no memos, and labels plain thematic coding as grounded theory.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when sampling was not iterative, when the theory is untested outside the data, and when a single coder worked alone (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a list of codes, a set of memos, and a theory built from the categories that the coding produced. It shows how each category in the theory links back to the codes and memos.

technique: **Document and policy analysis**
what_it_does: Reads documents systematically to extract facts, positions, changes or stated reasons, using their provenance and purpose. Artefact: an extraction table or chronology; read the author, audience and purpose before the content.
fit_test: It is used as proof of what happened in practice, when it shows only what an institution says or did.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** A commonly cited guidance paper (Bowen 2009) was recalled and not opened.
purpose: Reads documents systematically to extract facts, positions, changes or stated reasons using their provenance and purpose, and produces an extraction table or chronology.
use_when: Use when the question is what laws, reports or regulations say, when they changed, or why an institution says it acted.
document_genre: prefers=legal or regulatory text; prefers=government or agency report; prefers=organisation report
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The documents are used as proof of what happened in practice, when they show only what an institution says it did.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE-01 :: appraise each document before relying on its content; pairs with :: TC-04 :: extracted claims should be checked against the source text
typical_model_failure: Quotes text that is not in the document, or reads a stated reason as the true reason.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:repeat runs; decision-informing:prompt variation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:repeat runs; high-stakes:prompt variation; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; language model; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when documents are secondary or edited, when authorship and purpose are unknown, and when practice is inferred from policy (indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is an extraction table or chronology with one row per document, giving the facts, positions, changes or stated reasons found in it. Each row names the author, audience and purpose of the document, which are stated before its content.

technique: **Bibliometric analysis (citation analysis, science mapping, co-citation, co-word analysis)**
what_it_does: Counts and maps publications, authors and citations to show the structure and growth of a field. Artefact: performance tables and network maps; read clusters and trends, not single counts.
fit_test: The topic is small, the database covers the field poorly, or citation counts are read as quality.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** A guidelines paper was found in search results and not opened.
purpose: Counts and maps publications, authors and citations to show the structure and growth of a field and produces performance tables and network maps.
use_when: Use when you want to know who publishes on a topic, how it has grown and which clusters of work exist.
requires_minimum: a bibliographic export from a citation database
not_for_text: The topic is small, the database covers the field poorly, or citation counts are read as quality.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-03 :: duplicate publication records inflate counts; pairs with :: DM-21 :: network structure of authors or citations can be examined with social network analysis
typical_model_failure: Miscounts records, merges authors who share a name, and reads citation counts as a measure of quality.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:spot check; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:provenance log
error_sources: input data; data transformation; source selection
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with poor database coverage of the field (indirectness), name ambiguity, duplicated records and citation lags (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has performance tables of publications, authors and citations, and network maps of the field. It describes the clusters and trends shown by the maps and does not rest on single counts.

technique: **Trend and time-series decomposition** Also serves: Project forward.
what_it_does: Separates trend, seasonal and irregular parts of a series. Artefact: plots and a fitted trend; read breaks and seasonality.
fit_test: Definitions changed during the series.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** A forecasting textbook was listed and not opened.
purpose: Separates a series into trend, seasonal and irregular parts and produces plots and a fitted trend.
use_when: Use when you need to know whether a rising or falling series reflects a trend, a seasonal pattern or noise.
requires_minimum: at least two full seasonal cycles for seasonal decomposition
not_for_text: Definitions or measurement changed during the series, which produces false breaks.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-04 :: profile the series for gaps and definition changes first; pairs with :: PJ-01 :: decomposed components inform forecasting
typical_model_failure: Fits a decomposition by eye or in prose without running it, and reads a definition change as a trend break.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:spot check; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:provenance log
error_sources: input data; statistical assumptions; data transformation
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with short series, definition breaks and outliers (imprecision and risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has plots of the series and its separated trend, seasonal and irregular parts, with a fitted trend. It names the breaks in the series and the seasonal pattern.

technique: **Distribution, outlier and base-rate checks**
what_it_does: Examines the shape, extremes and baseline frequency of data before a figure is interpreted. Artefact: histograms, summary statistics, flagged outliers and a base rate; read whether the mean is representative and whether a rare event rate is high only against a small base.
fit_test: Outliers are deleted without cause.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** No single primary source was opened.
purpose: Examines the shape, extremes and baseline frequency of data before a figure is interpreted and produces histograms, summary statistics, flagged outliers and a base rate.
use_when: Use when you are about to quote a mean or a rare event rate and need to know whether it is representative and what the base is.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: Outliers are deleted without cause, or the summary replaces a look at the records behind it.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-04 :: profiling and rule-based validation catch format errors first; pairs with :: MM-02 :: algorithmic outlier detection extends the flagged outlier list
typical_model_failure: Describes distribution shape without computing it, and drops outliers that are real values.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:spot check; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:provenance log
error_sources: input data; data transformation; statistical assumptions
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the data are already aggregated, when outliers cannot be traced to records, or when no base rate is available (imprecision).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has histograms, summary statistics, a list of flagged outliers and a base rate for the data. It states whether the mean is representative and whether a rare event rate is high only against a small base.

technique: Grey literature appraisal checklist (AACODS (Authority, Accuracy, Coverage, Objectivity, Date, Significance))
what_it_does: Scores a non-peer-reviewed item on six criteria, each answered yes, no or unclear. Artefact: a completed checklist. Read the Objectivity and Accuracy answers for unstated bias and unsupported claims.
fit_test: Fits an item with no design-specific checklist. Misfit: the item is a study whose design has its own checklist. The checklist has no sponsorship item, so the analyst must record funder and author affiliations at the Authority and Objectivity steps.
status_and_evidence: Documented. Written by Tyndall at Flinders University in 2010, with no scoring rule or inclusion threshold. No study of its validity or reliability was found. ([AACODS checklist](https://oxfordhealth.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2024/01/AACODS_Checklist.pdf))
purpose: Scores a non-peer-reviewed item on six criteria (authority, accuracy, coverage, objectivity, date, significance) and produces a completed checklist.
use_when: Use when you must decide whether to rely on a government, organisation or consultancy report that has no design-specific checklist.
document_genre: requires=government or agency report; requires=organisation report; requires=news or commentary; requires=other
requires_minimum: none
not_for_rules: document_genre=research article|evidence synthesis :: a design-specific checklist applies to these genres
not_for_text: The item is a study whose design has its own checklist. The checklist has no sponsorship item, so record funder and author affiliations at the authority and objectivity steps.
related_techniques: substitutes for :: HE1-03 :: when document_genre is government or agency report or organisation report and a structured checklist is wanted; pairs with :: CM-01 :: funder and affiliation records support a comparison of sponsored and non-sponsored findings
typical_model_failure: Answers yes on authority and objectivity from the report's own claims, and does not record funder or affiliation.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:repeat runs; decision-informing:prompt variation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:repeat runs; high-stakes:prompt variation; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the checklist is read as a score (it has no scoring rule), when the funder is unknown, and when one assessor answers every item (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a completed checklist with one row per criterion (authority, accuracy, coverage, objectivity, date, significance), each answered yes, no or unclear. It states what the objectivity and accuracy answers show about unstated bias and unsupported claims.

technique: Critical appraisal checklist by study design (CASP (Critical Appraisal Skills Programme) checklists; JBI (Joanna Briggs Institute) checklists)
what_it_does: Answers design-specific questions on validity, results and relevance. JBI lists 15 checklists, including prevalence, analytical cross-sectional and qualitative studies and three for textual evidence (expert opinion, narrative, policy). Artefact: item answers. Read the validity items first.
fit_test: Choose the checklist by the design the study used. Neither source gives a scoring rule, and the items in the JBI textual evidence checklists were not read.
status_and_evidence: Documented. CASP describes its checklists as a guide and not a replacement for judgement. JBI gives no scoring rule on the page read. ([JBI critical appraisal tools](https://jbi.global/Critical-Appraisal-Tools); [CASP knowledge hub](https://casp-uk.net/knowledge-hub/))
purpose: Answers design-specific questions on validity, results and relevance for one study and produces a completed checklist for the evidence base.
use_when: Use when you need to judge how far to trust a single study, such as a randomised trial, a cohort study, a qualitative study or an expert opinion paper, and its design has a checklist.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The checklist does not match the design the study used. Neither source gives a scoring rule, so a summed score should not be used as a threshold.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE1-07 :: item answers feed the certainty rating; should follow :: HE1-08 :: appraisal applies to the included studies of a review
typical_model_failure: Picks the wrong checklist for the design, or answers items from the abstract without the methods section.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when items are answered from reports that omit methods, when one appraiser works alone, and when the checklist is turned into a score (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a list of answers to the checklist questions that fit the study design, with the validity items listed first and then the results and relevance items. Each answer is given beside its item.

technique: Appraisal of a systematic review (AMSTAR 2 (A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews 2); ROBIS (Risk Of Bias In Systematic reviews))
what_it_does: AMSTAR 2 rates confidence in a review from 16 items and seven critical domains as high, moderate, low or critically low. ROBIS rates concern in four domains and gives no summary score. Artefact: a rating or domain judgements. Read which critical items failed or which domains raise concern.
fit_test: Fits healthcare reviews of interventions. Misfit: a consultancy review that is not systematic. In one ROBIS pilot two reviewers agreed on 26 of 40 domain ratings (65 per cent). The Cochrane Handbook recommends neither instrument over the other.
status_and_evidence: Documented. ROBIS is not validated outside healthcare. ([AMSTAR 2, BMJ 2017](https://www.ortopaedi.dk/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/AMSTAR-2-original-artikel.pdf); [ROBIS, J Clin Epidemiol](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/132646/1/1_s2.0_S089543561500308X_main.pdf); [Cochrane Handbook chapter V](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-v))
purpose: Rates confidence in a systematic review with AMSTAR 2 (high to critically low) or concern in four domains with ROBIS, and produces a rating or domain judgements.
use_when: Use when you need to decide whether a published systematic review can be relied on.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The review is not systematic, such as a consultancy review, or it does not concern healthcare interventions (ROBIS is not validated outside healthcare). Assessors can disagree: in one pilot two reviewers agreed on 26 of 40 domain ratings.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE-07 :: each review in an overview needs this appraisal; pairs with :: HE1-07 :: the review rating feeds certainty of a body of evidence
typical_model_failure: Rates critical items as met without reading the methods, and gives a single score for ROBIS, which has none.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with low inter-assessor agreement, a single assessor, and application outside healthcare (indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a confidence rating of high, moderate, low or critically low for the review, or a judgement of concern for each of the four domains, depending on the tool used. It names the critical items that failed or the domains that raise concern.

technique: Survey disclosure completeness check (AAPOR (American Association for Public Opinion Research) disclosure elements)
what_it_does: Tests whether a survey report states the sponsor, question wording, population, sampling frame, mode, dates, sample size, margin of error and weighting. Artefact: a list of disclosed and missing items. Read each missing item as a finding.
fit_test: Fits any publicly released survey. It tests disclosure, not accuracy.
status_and_evidence: Documented. The standards list what must be disclosed at release and what must be supplied on request within 30 days. ([AAPOR disclosure standards](https://www.aapor.org/standards-ethics/disclosure-standards/))
purpose: Tests whether a survey report states the sponsor, question wording, population, sampling frame, mode, dates, sample size, margin of error and weighting, and produces a list of disclosed and missing items.
use_when: Use when you want to know whether a published survey gives enough information to be assessed.
document_genre: prefers=organisation report; prefers=government or agency report; prefers=news or commentary
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The aim is to judge accuracy. The check tests disclosure, not whether the survey is right.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE-05 :: disclosed sampling method decides which margin of error is valid; pairs with :: HE-06 :: disclosed mode and panel type point to the respondent quality check
typical_model_failure: Marks an element as disclosed because the report uses a related word, and does not read each missing item as a finding.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:repeat runs; decision-informing:prompt variation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:repeat runs; high-stakes:prompt variation; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the source report is a press summary and the full methods statement exists elsewhere (reporting bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a list of the items the survey report should disclose (sponsor, question wording, population, sampling frame, mode, dates, sample size, margin of error and weighting), each marked as disclosed or missing. Each missing item is stated as a finding.

technique: Margin of error and credibility interval check
what_it_does: Checks that a reported margin of error matches the sampling method. Artefact: a judgement on whether the figure is valid. Read the sampling type first, because a margin of sampling error applies to probability samples and opt-in polls report model-based credibility intervals that depend on assumptions.
fit_test: Fits any reported survey precision. The rule is mechanical, but judging the assumptions behind a credibility interval needs a person.
status_and_evidence: Documented. The source is a statement of position and not an experiment. ([AAPOR statement on credibility intervals](https://aapor.org/statements/understanding-a-credibility-interval-and-how-it-differs-from-the-margin-of-sampling-error-in-a-public-opinion-poll/))
purpose: Checks that a reported margin of error matches the sampling method and produces a judgement on whether the figure is valid.
use_when: Use when a poll or survey reports a margin of error and you need to know whether that figure means what it says.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: Judging the assumptions behind a model-based credibility interval needs a person, even though the rule for probability samples is mechanical.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE-04 :: the disclosure check supplies the sampling type
typical_model_failure: Accepts a margin of sampling error for an opt-in poll, where only a model-based credibility interval can apply.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; statistical assumptions
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the sampling type is not disclosed or the model behind a credibility interval is not stated (reporting bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a judgement on whether the reported margin of error is valid for the sampling method. It names the sampling type first and says whether the figure is a margin of sampling error or a model-based credibility interval that depends on assumptions.

technique: Opt-in panel respondent quality check (bogus respondent screen)
what_it_does: Looks for implausible answers that show careless or fraudulent respondents inflating rare responses. Artefact: a judgement of inflation risk. Read results for under-30 and Hispanic subgroups in opt-in samples first, the subgroups Pew found affected.
fit_test: Fits opt-in online surveys. Pew found few implausible answers in probability panels. Its finding comes from one study of six samples and may not apply to business panels.
status_and_evidence: Documented. 12 per cent of opt-in respondents under 30 claimed a licence to operate a nuclear submarine, against a true share that rounds to 0 per cent. ([Pew Research Center 2024](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2024/03/05/online-opt-in-polls-can-produce-misleading-results-especially-for-young-people-and-hispanic-adults/))
purpose: Looks for implausible answers that show careless or fraudulent respondents inflating rare responses in an opt-in survey and produces a judgement of inflation risk.
use_when: Use when an opt-in online survey reports a rare behaviour or a result for a young or minority subgroup that looks too high.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The survey uses a probability panel, where few implausible answers were found. The supporting finding comes from one study of six samples and may not apply to business panels.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE-04 :: the disclosure check shows the panel type and mode
typical_model_failure: Flags real but unusual respondents as bogus, and does not compare rates with a probability sample.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:repeat runs; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:repeat runs; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; statistical assumptions
certainty_limits: Certainty drops because the evidence base is one study and results for subgroups are imprecise (imprecision and indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a judgement of the risk that careless or fraudulent respondents have inflated rare responses, with the implausible answers that support it. It reports the results for the under-30 and Hispanic subgroups first when the sample is opt-in.

technique: Overview of reviews (umbrella review; tertiary review)
what_it_does: Uses systematic reviews, not primary studies, as the unit of search, inclusion and analysis. Artefact: a summary of reviews with a quality rating per review and an overlap map. Read the citation matrix and the corrected covered area for double counting of primary studies.
fit_test: Fits when several reviews exist. Misfit: primary studies are missing from the reviews, or network meta-analysis is needed. Rarely suited to ranking interventions.
status_and_evidence: Documented. Constrained by the quality and currency of the included reviews. The first 100,000 of about 117,000 characters of the chapter were read. ([Cochrane Handbook chapter V](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-v))
purpose: Uses systematic reviews as the unit of search, inclusion and analysis and produces a summary of reviews with a quality rating per review and an overlap map.
use_when: Use when several systematic reviews already cover a question and you need one summary across them.
requires_minimum: at least two systematic reviews on the question
not_for_text: Primary studies are missing from the reviews, or a network meta-analysis is needed. It is rarely suited to ranking interventions.
related_techniques: should follow :: HE-03 :: rate each included review first; should follow :: HE1-08 :: the method follows systematic review search and screening conventions
typical_model_failure: Counts a primary study several times because it appears in several reviews, and skips the overlap matrix.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; source selection; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with overlap between reviews, reviews that are out of date, and reviews of low quality (risk of bias and indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a summary of reviews with one row per review, giving a quality rating for each, and an overlap map of the primary studies shared between reviews. It includes the citation matrix and the corrected covered area as the measure of double counting.

technique: Living systematic review
what_it_does: Keeps a review continuously updated as new studies appear. Artefact: a versioned evidence summary and an update log. Read the date of the last search.
fit_test: Fits fast-moving topics where new studies keep arriving. The page read gives no limits.
status_and_evidence: Documented. Definition only; operating demands were not confirmed. ([Elliott et al., PLoS Medicine 2014](https://doaj.org/article/8607f0c7a9e04b76bbf74150eef39ab2))
purpose: Keeps a systematic review continuously updated as new studies appear and produces a versioned evidence summary and an update log.
use_when: Use when a topic moves fast and a review would be out of date by the time it is used.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The topic is stable, so updates add effort without changing the answer. The page read gives no operating limits.
related_techniques: should follow :: HE1-08 :: an existing systematic review is the baseline to update
typical_model_failure: States the date of the last search from memory and does not log which new studies were screened out.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; source selection; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the date of the last search is unclear, and when updates change inclusion rules (reporting bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a versioned evidence summary with an update log that lists each change as new studies were added. It states the date of the last search.

technique: **Trend extrapolation and time-series forecasting (exponential smoothing, autoregressive integrated moving average models, trend impact analysis)**
what_it_does: Extends the measured historical path of an indicator using a stated functional form. Artefact: a central projection with prediction intervals; read interval width and compare with a naive no-change forecast.
fit_test: The series is short or its definition changed, the projection does not beat a naive benchmark in back-testing, no interval is stated, or the driver of the trend is reaching a limit.
status_and_evidence: **Unconfirmed.** Forecasting competition results and the Principles of Forecasting were recalled, and the page failed to load. The note author expects the strongest accuracy base here, limited to stable quantities, but this was not verified.
purpose: Extend the measured history of one indicator with a stated functional form to give a central projection with prediction intervals, as a draft result.
use_when: Use when you need a forward projection of a stable quantity that has a long, consistently defined history and a stated horizon.
requires_minimum: A series with a constant definition and enough periods to cover at least two full seasonal cycles where seasonality exists, plus a stated horizon.
not_for_text: The series is short or its definition changed, no interval is stated, or the driver of the trend is reaching a limit.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-04 :: a data quality report shows definition breaks and gaps in the series before it is extended; pairs with :: PJ-02 :: base rates from similar cases test whether the extrapolated path is plausible; pairs with :: PJ-07 :: an S-curve fit covers the case where the trend approaches a ceiling
typical_model_failure: Extends the trend by eye or in text arithmetic and omits the prediction interval and the comparison with a naive no-change forecast.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:held-out validation; decision-informing:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:held-out validation; high-stakes:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:leakage check; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions; high-stakes:assumption and limitation statement
error_sources: input data; statistical assumptions
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when back-testing does not beat a naive benchmark (indirectness), the series is short or changed definition (risk of bias), or the interval is wide (imprecision).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a central projection of the indicator with prediction intervals, based on a stated functional form. It gives the interval width and a comparison with a naive no-change forecast.

technique: **Reference class forecasting (outside view, base-rate forecasting)** Also serves: Compare.
what_it_does: Replaces a bottom-up estimate with the distribution of outcomes in similar past cases. Artefact: a distribution of outcomes and the case's position within it; read the base rate first, then justify departures.
fit_test: The class was chosen after seeing the answer, has only a handful of cases, or several plausible classes give very different base rates that are not reported.
status_and_evidence: **Tested.** In the Good Judgment Project, use of comparison classes was the only principle significantly correlated with forecasting success, as summarised by a blog (secondary). PMI describes the three steps and the method's limits where few precedents exist. ([AI Impacts, summary of Good Judgment Project research](https://aiimpacts.org/?p=1260); [PMI, From Nobel Prize to project management: reference class forecasting](https://www.pmi.org/learning/library/nobel-project-management-reference-class-forecasting-8068))
purpose: Replace a bottom-up estimate with the distribution of outcomes in similar completed cases, giving a base-rate distribution and the case position in it as a draft result.
use_when: Use when you are asked how long, how much or how likely for a project or event that has many comparable precedents with recorded outcomes.
requires_minimum: Enough completed comparable cases to form a distribution, not a handful; the case count is reported with the result.
not_for_text: The reference class was chosen after seeing the answer, has only a handful of cases, or several plausible classes give very different base rates that are not reported.
related_techniques: pairs with :: PJ-01 :: the outside view tests a trend extrapolation against outcomes of similar cases; pairs with :: CK-15 :: a representativeness audit tests whether the chosen class covers comparable cases
typical_model_failure: Picks a reference class that already matches the preferred answer and reports one base rate without showing the rates from other plausible classes.
minimum_checks: exploratory:assumption and limitation statement; decision-informing:assumption and limitation statement; decision-informing:sensitivity analysis; decision-informing:code execution for arithmetic; high-stakes:assumption and limitation statement; high-stakes:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:code execution for arithmetic; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; source selection; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the class has few cases (imprecision), when plausible classes disagree (inconsistency), or when past cases differ from the present case in ways that matter (indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a distribution of outcomes in similar past cases and the position of the case within that distribution. It states the base rate first and then gives the justification for any departure from it.

technique: **Forecasting tournaments and superforecasting practice**
what_it_does: Produces dated probability estimates for resolvable questions, scores them with Brier scores and improves them by training, teaming, updating and aggregation. Artefact: a probability record and score; read calibration and resolution.
fit_test: The question cannot be resolved by a dated observable outcome, the horizon is long, forecasts are stated in words only, or nothing is scored.
status_and_evidence: **Tested.** See the evidence section for effect sizes and caveats. ([AI Impacts, summary of Good Judgment Project research](https://aiimpacts.org/?p=1260); [Wikipedia, Superforecaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superforecaster))
purpose: Produce dated probability estimates for resolvable questions, score them with Brier scores and improve them by updating and aggregation, leaving a scored probability record as a draft result.
use_when: Use when you need calibrated probabilities for questions that will resolve on a dated, observable outcome and forecasters can update over time.
requires_minimum: A question with a resolution date and criterion, one forecaster or a team, access to news and data, a scoring rule and repeated updating over time.
not_for_text: The question cannot be resolved by a dated observable outcome, the horizon is long, forecasts are stated in words only, or nothing is scored.
related_techniques: pairs with :: TC1-14 :: coherence correction and averaging improve the probabilities of several forecasters; pairs with :: CM1-13 :: comparing forecasters against resolved outcomes shows which are calibrated
typical_model_failure: States a single probability once without dates, updates or a scoring rule, which cannot be calibrated.
minimum_checks: exploratory:assumption and limitation statement; decision-informing:assumption and limitation statement; decision-informing:code execution for arithmetic; decision-informing:provenance log; high-stakes:assumption and limitation statement; high-stakes:code execution for arithmetic; high-stakes:provenance log; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: expert opinion; input data
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when few questions have resolved (imprecision), when the horizon is long (indirectness), or when forecasters share information or views (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a probability record with one row per question, giving the date, the probability estimate and, once resolved, the outcome and the Brier score. It reports calibration and resolution.

technique: **Delphi technique (real-time Delphi, mini-Delphi)**
what_it_does: Collects anonymous expert estimates over two or more rounds with controlled feedback. Artefact: median and interquartile range per round; treat persistent disagreement as information.
fit_test: The panel is a convenience sample with similar views, no feedback is given between rounds, or consensus is reported as accuracy.
status_and_evidence: **Documented.** Rowe and Wright (1999) report few validation studies, often without a description of conditions, so it is hard to identify which aspects relate to accuracy. The UK Futures Toolkit lists it, which shows use, not accuracy. what_it_does: Models how an adversary or other actor would decide by reasoning in that actor's first-person voice (CIA), or examines a plan from outside the planning team (UK). Artefact: first-person memos predicting decisions; read decisions that differ from the home team's expectation.
fit_test: The analysts cannot escape their own mindsets, or an external team is misused to attack the plan.

technique: **High-impact and low-probability analysis** Also serves: Project forward.
what_it_does: Works out plausible pathways to an unlikely but consequential event, with triggers and indicators. Artefact: pathways and indicators; read indicators that can be watched cheaply.

([CIA Tradecraft Primer (2009)](https://www.cia.gov/resources/csi/static/Tradecraft-Primer-apr09.pdf); [UK Red Teaming Handbook](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1027158/20210625-Red_Teaming_Handbook.pdf))

not_for_text: The event is not high impact, or pathways are too vague to produce indicators.

purpose: Assumes an unexpected event has occurred, explains how it could have come about, and produces scenarios with indicators and consequence assessments.
use_when: Use when the conventional view excludes an event and you want to test how it could arise and what follows.
requires_minimum: The conventional line and an assumed event.
not_for_text: The narrative describes only the outcome and not the causal chain.

technique: **Premortem (prospective hindsight, inversion)** Also serves: Project forward.
what_it_does: Asks a team to assume the plan has already failed and to write the reasons. Artefact: a ranked or grouped list of failure reasons; read clusters and reasons raised only by sceptical members.

status_and_evidence: **Practice.** Described by Klein in 2007; the commonly quoted effect figure from Mitchell, Russo and Pennington (1989) is unconfirmed, and no evidence of improved outcomes was found. ([Klein, Performing a project premortem, Harvard Business Review](https://hbr.org/2007/09/performing-a-project-premortem); [Wikipedia, Pre-mortem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-mortem))
purpose: Asks a team to assume the plan has already failed and to write the reasons, and produces a grouped list of failure reasons and draft assumptions.
use_when: Use when a plan is about to be adopted and you want the team to say why it might fail while it can still change.

not_for_text: It is run after the decision has been taken, or reasons are not converted into plan changes or monitored indicators.

technique: **Structured self-critique**
what_it_does: Asks about sources of uncertainty, evidence, gaps, critical assumptions and alternative hypotheses. Artefact: a written critique of one's own analysis.

purpose: Asks about sources of uncertainty, evidence, gaps, critical assumptions and alternative hypotheses, and produces a written critique of one own analysis.
use_when: Use when you have drafted an analysis and want to find its gaps and weak assumptions before it is reviewed by others.
requires_minimum: A draft analysis.
not_for_text: It is applied dishonestly, since the handbook says it is only as good as the honesty with which it is applied.

technique: **Rapoport's rules (fair restatement of an opposing position)** Also serves: Compare.
what_it_does: Requires the analyst to restate the opposing position fairly, list points of agreement and what was learned, and only then rebut. Artefact: a restatement and an agreement list; the remaining disagreements are the real ones.
fit_test: The opponent would not accept the restatement as well expressed. It is a debate procedure and does not show which position is correct (inference).
status_and_evidence: **Documented.** Summarised from Dennett's 2013 account of Rapoport (1960) on a secondary page. ([Wikipedia, Rapoport's rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapoport%27s_rules))
purpose: Requires a fair restatement of the opposing position, a list of points of agreement and of what was learned before any rebuttal, and produces a restatement and an agreement list.
use_when: Use when two sides talk past each other and you want to find the disagreements that remain once each side has been stated fairly.
requires_minimum: The strongest available statement of the opposing view, from its proponents.
not_for_text: The opponent would not accept the restatement as well expressed. It is a debate procedure and does not show which position is correct.
consumes: charter or question:agreed; raw dataset or corpus:raw; result:draft
related_techniques: pairs with :: CH-11 :: Steelmanning goes further by strengthening the opposing position; pairs with :: CH-04 :: Team A and Team B debates start from fair statements of each case
typical_model_failure: Restates the opposing position in the analyst own terms, which the opponent would not accept.

error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement; language model
certainty_limits: Summarised from a secondary account; whether the opponent accepts the restatement is the only test, and it is not run by the technique alone.

technique: **Steelmanning** Also serves: Compare.
what_it_does: Builds the strongest version of a position the analyst disagrees with, then responds to it. Artefact: a strengthened opposing argument and a response, which tests the analyst's own position.
fit_test: The strengthened version is no longer recognisable as the opponent's position, or adds claims the opponent rejects.
status_and_evidence: **Practice.** Described on encyclopaedia pages with no evidence that it works better than other techniques. ([Wikipedia, Steelmanning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steelmanning); [Wikipedia, Straw man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straw_man))

use_when: Use when you want to test your own position against the best form of the opposing argument and not a weak version.
requires_minimum: The opposing argument and enough domain knowledge to repair its weak assumptions.
not_for_text: The strengthened version is no longer recognisable as the opponent position, or adds claims the opponent rejects.
consumes: charter or question:agreed; raw dataset or corpus:raw; result:draft
related_techniques: pairs with :: CH-10 :: Fair restatement keeps the strengthened version faithful to what the opponent holds; pairs with :: CH-03 :: Devil advocacy argues against the plan using the strengthened case
typical_model_failure: Adds claims the opponent does not hold, or strengthens the position in a way that makes it easy to answer.

error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement; language model
certainty_limits: No evidence that it works better than other techniques; the result depends on the analyst domain knowledge to repair weak assumptions.

output_spec: The result has two parts: the opposing position restated in its strongest form, and a response to that restated version. It must keep the restated position recognisable to its holder and end with a statement of what the response shows about the analyst's own position.

fit_test: The author's answers change the claim itself.

use_when: Use when a stated position is unclear or may rest on hidden assumptions and a partner can question the author.
requires_minimum: A stated position and a partner or a written list of question types.
not_for_text: The author answers change the claim itself.
consumes: charter or question:agreed; raw dataset or corpus:raw; result:draft
related_techniques: pairs with :: TC1-23 :: The ladder of inference gives the steps to question; pairs with :: CH-01 :: A key assumptions check tests the hidden assumptions that questioning exposes

technique: **Cognitive bias checks and debiasing (including consider-the-opposite)**

use_when: Use when a conclusion has been reached and you want to check which known biases may have shaped it.
requires_minimum: A conclusion, its process and a bias list.
not_for_text: The check is run after the conclusion is fixed.
related_techniques: pairs with :: TC1-16 :: A search for disconfirming evidence follows each marked item; pairs with :: CH-09 :: Structured self-critique covers the same ground with open questions
typical_model_failure: Marks every bias as possible in general terms without linking any to a step in the actual reasoning.
minimum_checks: exploratory:assumption and limitation statement; decision-informing:assumption and limitation statement; decision-informing:independent review; high-stakes:assumption and limitation statement; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:expert review; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement; language model
certainty_limits: Only an abstract of a review was read and effect evidence was not confirmed; debiasing has barriers to real-world effectiveness, so certainty is lowered by indirectness.

technique: **Structured brainstorming**

([CIA Tradecraft Primer (2009)](https://www.cia.gov/resources/csi/static/Tradecraft-Primer-apr09.pdf); [UK Red Teaming Handbook](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1027158/20210625-Red_Teaming_Handbook.pdf))

use_when: Use when you need a wide set of ideas, causes or options on a focal question before narrowing.

not_for_text: Individuals cannot escape their own biases, and productivity falls after about 60 to 90 minutes.

error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement; language model
