what_it_does: Controls how a group forms views: each person contributes in turn with seniors last, leaders withhold early preferences, and evaluators rotate. Artefact: independent individual views.

status_and_evidence: **Documented.** Described in the UK handbook, which presents no effectiveness evidence for its techniques. ([UK Red Teaming Handbook](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1027158/20210625-Red_Teaming_Handbook.pdf))

use_when: Use when a group may defer to its senior member or converge too early and you want independent views recorded first.
requires_minimum: A group and a facilitator.
not_for_text: The devil advocate role becomes cumbersome, as noted for mindguarding.

typical_model_failure: Simulates several group members with one model, which gives one view under several names and defeats the independence the technique protects.

error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement; language model
certainty_limits: The source presents no effectiveness evidence for its techniques; independence depends on the facilitator and on how the group is run.

output_spec: The result has one independent view per person, recorded before any group discussion, with the contributor named against each view. It states the order in which people contributed and who withheld an early preference.

technique: Corpus construction and sampling (document selection; search string design; sampling frame design)
what_it_does: Defines which documents enter the analysis, so that counts and themes describe a stated population. Artefact: a corpus table with counts per source, period and document type, and an inclusion log. Read coverage, imbalance and gaps before reading any result.
fit_test: Test: name the population the corpus represents and count documents per source and period. Misfit: the corpus is whatever was easiest to retrieve, one source supplies most documents, or the search string contains the conclusion terms. For a fixed coding budget, code more unique documents instead of using more coders per document.
status_and_evidence: Documented. Representation is the first of five tasks in the text-as-data framework; the coding-budget result is from an abstract. ([Barberá et al. 2021 via EconPapers](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:cup:polals:v:29:y:2021:i:1:p:19-42_2); [Stanford Political Science: Text as Data](https://politicalscience.stanford.edu/publications/text-data-new-framework-machine-learning-and-social-sciences))
purpose: Define which documents enter the analysis so that counts and themes describe a stated population, giving a corpus table with counts and an inclusion log.
use_when: Use when you are about to count or code documents and must decide which documents represent the population you are asking about.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The corpus is whatever was easiest to retrieve, one source supplies most documents, or the search string contains the conclusion terms.
produces: raw dataset or corpus:raw; screening log:complete; data source inventory:draft; training sample:drawn; held-out test sample:sealed
related_techniques: pairs with :: CK-15 :: a representativeness audit tests whether the corpus covers the stated population; pairs with :: PE-03 :: removing near-duplicates after selection stops repeats counting as separate documents
typical_model_failure: Treats the supplied documents as the whole population and overstates themes drawn from a few documents.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:code execution for arithmetic; decision-informing:provenance log; decision-informing:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:code execution for arithmetic; high-stakes:provenance log; high-stakes:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:human review sample
error_sources: input data; source selection; coder or rater judgement
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when one source supplies most documents (risk of bias), when coverage by period or type is uneven (indirectness), or when the search string reflects the expected answer (reporting bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a corpus table with one row per source, period and document type, giving the document count in each, followed by an inclusion log listing what was included or excluded and why. It names the population the corpus represents and ends with the coverage gaps and imbalances.

technique: Preprocessing sensitivity testing (text cleaning; tokenisation; stopword removal; stemming; boilerplate removal; preText)
what_it_does: Converts raw text into countable units and re-runs the main result under several defensible cleaning regimes. Artefact: cleaned text or a document-term matrix, a log of every rule, and a sensitivity result. Read whether themes or rankings change across regimes.
fit_test: Use before any unsupervised model. A finding that changes across regimes is unstable. Whether neural embedding methods are equally sensitive was not confirmed.
status_and_evidence: Tested. Preprocessing choices have "profound effects on the results of real models for real data" (abstract); the authors propose preText to measure the sensitivity. ([Denny and Spirling 2018, Political Analysis](https://cambridge.org/core/journals/political-analysis/article/abs/text-preprocessing-for-unsupervised-learning-why-it-matters-when-it-misleads-and-what-to-do-about-it/AA7D4DE0AA6AB208502515AE3EC6989E))
purpose: Convert raw text into countable units and re-run the main result under several defensible cleaning regimes, giving cleaned text, a document-term matrix, a rule log and a sensitivity result.
use_when: Use when you are about to count words or run an unsupervised model on raw text and need to know whether cleaning choices change the result.
requires_minimum: A tokeniser and stopword list for the language of the text.
not_for_text: Whether neural embedding methods are equally sensitive to cleaning was not confirmed, so the technique may add little before an embedding method.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-03 :: removing near-duplicates first stops repeats distorting counts; pairs with :: MM-12 :: preprocessing sensitivity tests the stability of a topic model result; pairs with :: MM-14 :: document clustering results can change with the cleaning rules
typical_model_failure: Applies one cleaning rule set without recording it, so the result cannot be reproduced.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:provenance log; decision-informing:spot check; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:provenance log; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; data transformation
certainty_limits: A finding that changes across cleaning regimes is unstable and its certainty drops (inconsistency); the regimes tried may not cover the defensible ones (reporting bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has the cleaned text or document-term matrix, a log listing every cleaning rule applied, and a sensitivity table showing the main result under each cleaning regime. It ends by stating whether the themes or rankings changed across regimes.

technique: Near-duplicate detection (shingling; MinHash; locality-sensitive hashing; text reuse detection)
what_it_does: Finds identical or nearly identical documents so repeats are not counted as independent evidence. Artefact: duplicate clusters with similarity scores. Read cluster sizes, because a large cluster means syndicated or copied content.
fit_test: Fits sources that syndicate or republish. A low threshold merges distinct documents and a high one leaves rewrites, and banding gives false positives that need direct checking.
status_and_evidence: Documented. Course slides describe shingles of length 8 to 10 and MinHash estimation of Jaccard similarity. One 61-word sentence appeared over 60,000 times in a language model training set, and deduplication reduced memorised output about tenfold. ([Stanford CS246 LSH slides](https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs246/slides/03-lsh.pdf); [Lee et al. 2022, arXiv 2107.06499](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.06499))
purpose: Find identical or nearly identical documents so repeats are not counted as independent evidence, giving duplicate clusters with similarity scores and a deduplicated corpus.
use_when: Use when sources syndicate, copy or republish and you need to stop repeated content counting as separate evidence.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: Documents are all original with no republishing, or the similarity threshold cannot be checked by reading sample pairs.
related_techniques: pairs with :: IS-06 :: copy detection across sources estimates which sources depend on each other; pairs with :: PJ-23 :: removing repeated reports keeps signals independent
typical_model_failure: Merges distinct documents at a low threshold, or leaves rewrites unmatched at a high one, without checking sample pairs.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:provenance log
error_sources: input data; data transformation
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the threshold has not been tested on sample pairs (imprecision) or when banding produces false positives that are not checked directly (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a table of duplicate clusters, one row per cluster, giving the member documents, the cluster size and the similarity score. It ends with the largest clusters named as likely syndicated or copied content.

technique: Data profiling and rule-based validation (data audit; data quality assessment; edit checks)
what_it_does: Describes the structure, completeness, validity and consistency of each field and tests explicit rules such as end date after start date. Artefact: a profile table per column and a list of records that break each rule. Read for missing patterns, impossible values, duplicate keys and inconsistent codes.
fit_test: Always applicable as a first step. Profiling shows that a value is odd, not that it is wrong. The analyst chooses the rule set, and it is never complete.
status_and_evidence: Documented. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) framework defines seven quality dimensions. RADAR names five artefact classes: missing data, bad values, outliers, inconsistent formatting and inconsistent logic. The column profile layout is practice with no authoritative definition. ([ABS data quality framework](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/detailed-methodology-information/concepts-sources-methods/australian-system-government-finance-statistics-concepts-sources-and-methods/2015/16-data-quality/part-b-abs-data-quality-framework); [RADAR, arXiv 2506.08249](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.08249))
purpose: Describe the structure, completeness, validity and consistency of each field and test explicit rules, giving a profile table per column and a list of records that break each rule.
use_when: Use when you have received a table or dataset and need to know its quality before any analysis.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The profile is read as proof that a value is wrong; it shows only that a value is unusual, and the rule set chosen by the analyst is never complete.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE1-21 :: distribution and outlier checks examine the shape of values that profiling flags; pairs with :: MM-02 :: algorithmic outlier detection finds unusual values that explicit rules miss
typical_model_failure: Reports that odd values are errors and writes a short rule set as if it were complete.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:provenance log; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:provenance log; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; data transformation
certainty_limits: Certainty about quality drops when the rule set is short (reporting bias) or when field definitions are undocumented (indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a profile table with one row per column, giving its type, completeness, valid range and consistency, and a list of the records that break each stated rule. It ends by naming the missing patterns, impossible values, duplicate keys and inconsistent codes found.

technique: Missing data diagnosis and treatment (missingness analysis; imputation; complete case analysis; non-response weighting)
what_it_does: Measures how much is missing, where and for whom, then chooses deletion, imputation or weighting. Artefact: the missing share by field and subgroup, and a comparison of complete and incomplete cases. Read for systematic patterns.
fit_test: Fits when the missing share is similar across subgroups and unrelated to key variables. Misfit: missingness differs by outcome or group, so deletion biases results. The mechanism needs a person. The classification into missing completely at random, at random and not at random was not confirmed from a source.
status_and_evidence: Documented. The ABS states that imputation and weighting are the two standard treatments of non-response. ([ABS Methodological News, Dec 2009](https://www.abs.gov.au/AUSSTATS/abs@.nsf/Lookup/1504.0Main+Features6Dec+2009))
purpose: Measure how much is missing, where and for whom, then choose deletion, imputation or weighting, giving the missing share by field and subgroup and a cleaned dataset.
use_when: Use when records have blank or absent values and you must decide how to treat them before analysis.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: Missingness differs by outcome or group so deletion would bias results, or no person can judge why values are missing.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-04 :: profiling locates the missing values and their patterns; pairs with :: MM-06 :: survey weighting is the alternative treatment for non-response in survey records
typical_model_failure: Drops incomplete records or imputes means without testing whether missingness is related to the outcome.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:sensitivity analysis; decision-informing:spot check; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions; high-stakes:provenance log; high-stakes:expert review
error_sources: input data; data transformation; statistical assumptions
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the missingness mechanism cannot be judged (indirectness), when complete and incomplete cases differ (risk of bias), or when results change between treatments (inconsistency).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a table of the missing share by field and by subgroup, and a comparison of complete and incomplete cases. It names the fields where missingness follows a systematic pattern and states the treatment chosen: deletion, imputation or weighting.

technique: Keyword in context (KWIC; concordance)
what_it_does: Lists every occurrence of a keyword or phrase with a fixed number of surrounding words. Artefact: a table of document, position, preceding words, keyword and following words. Read how the term is used and whether use differs by source or period.
fit_test: Use it to check what a frequent or surprising term means before counting it. It is a reading aid, not a measurement. Reading only the first matches is the common misuse.
status_and_evidence: Documented. In the quanteda software the default window is 5 words, and the pattern can be a phrase, wildcard or regular expression. ([quanteda kwic reference](https://quanteda.io/reference/kwic.html))
purpose: List every occurrence of a keyword or phrase with a fixed number of surrounding words, giving a table of document, position and context.
use_when: Use when a frequent or surprising term needs checking for how it is used before it is counted or coded.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The context table is used as a measurement of frequency or sentiment, or only the first matches are read.
related_techniques: pairs with :: PE-07 :: collocations suggest the terms whose use should be read in context; pairs with :: MM-07 :: reading dictionary terms in context checks that they carry the intended meaning
typical_model_failure: Reads only the first few matches and reports a pattern of use for the whole corpus.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:source-span citation
error_sources: input data; data transformation
certainty_limits: Certainty about usage drops when only part of the matches are read (reporting bias) or when the window is too short to show meaning (indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a table with one row per occurrence of the keyword, giving the document, the position, the preceding words, the keyword and the following words. It ends with a statement of how the term is used and whether use differs by source or period.

technique: Collocation and n-gram extraction (phrase detection; association measures)
what_it_does: Finds word sequences that occur together more often than chance. Artefact: ranked phrases with association scores. Read recurring named concepts, fixed expressions and repeated boilerplate.
fit_test: Use to find multi-word terms before dictionary or topic work. Boilerplate and repeated headers produce top-ranked phrases. A low default minimum count means rare sequences are scored.
status_and_evidence: Documented. In quanteda the score is a lambda statistic with a Wald z value, the default minimum count is 2 and the default size is 2. ([quanteda textstat_collocations](https://quanteda.io/reference/textstat_collocations.html))
purpose: Find word sequences that occur together more often than chance, giving ranked phrases with association scores as a feature set.
use_when: Use when you need to find multi-word terms and fixed expressions before dictionary or topic work.
requires_minimum: A minimum phrase count set above the default of 2 for the size of the corpus.
not_for_text: Repeated headers and boilerplate have not been removed, so they would rank as the top phrases.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-02 :: cleaning and boilerplate removal stop repeated headers ranking as phrases; pairs with :: PE-06 :: reading top phrases in context shows what they mean
typical_model_failure: Reports boilerplate and repeated headers as recurring concepts.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; data transformation; statistical assumptions
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the minimum count is low so rare sequences are scored (imprecision) or when boilerplate remains (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a ranked list of phrases with an association score for each. It names the recurring concepts, fixed expressions and repeated boilerplate among them.

technique: Named entity recognition (NER; entity extraction)
what_it_does: Tags spans of text as people, organisations, places, dates and other types. Artefact: a table of mentions with type and position. Read which actors recur and in what contexts.
fit_test: Entity types must match the question. Domain terms, such as company names in filings or agency names in policy documents, are often mistagged. No domain accuracy figures were verified.
status_and_evidence: Documented. A textbook chapter on sequence labelling for named entities is listed on the contents page; the chapter was not opened. ([Jurafsky and Martin, SLP3 contents](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/))
purpose: Tag spans of text as people, organisations, places, dates and other types, giving a table of mentions with type and position and a tagged corpus.
use_when: Use when you need to know which people, organisations or places are named in a body of text and in what contexts.
requires_minimum: A tagger or model for the language of the text, and entity types that match the question.
not_for_text: Domain terms such as company names in filings or agency names in policy documents are likely to be mistagged and the entity types do not fit the question.
related_techniques: pairs with :: IS-01 :: entity resolution joins mentions of one entity that appear under different names; pairs with :: CK-04 :: a gold-standard sample measures tagging accuracy for the domain; should follow :: PE-03 :: removing repeated documents stops one mention being counted many times
typical_model_failure: Tags domain terms with the wrong type and treats each distinct spelling of a name as a separate entity.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; decision-informing:gold standard agreement; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:gold standard agreement; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:provenance log
error_sources: input data; statistical assumptions; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when accuracy has not been measured for the domain (indirectness), when entity types do not fit the question (indirectness), or when names vary (inconsistency).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a table of mentions, one row per mention, giving the text span, the entity type and the position. It ends with the actors that recur and the contexts in which they appear.

technique: Relation and event extraction (information extraction; open information extraction; temporal expression extraction)
what_it_does: Extracts who did what to whom, with arguments and time, as structured rows. Artefact: an event or relation table. Read counts by type and actor, and check a sample of rows against the source sentence.
fit_test: The schema must be fixed before extraction. Misfit: the schema changes between documents, or one event reported by five outlets is counted five times.
status_and_evidence: Tested. Open-weight models of 7 to 12 billion parameters followed event codebooks poorly zero-shot on protest and political violence coding, and supervised instruction tuning helped substantially (abstract, 2024). ([Halterman and Keith, arXiv 2407.10747](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10747v2); [Jurafsky and Martin, SLP3 contents](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/))
purpose: Extract who did what to whom, with arguments and time, as structured rows, giving an event or relation table and a coded corpus.
use_when: Use when you need counts of events or relations between actors and the source text reports them in sentences.
requires_minimum: A fixed schema of event or relation types written before extraction.
not_for_text: The schema changes between documents, or one event reported by several outlets would be counted as several events.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-03 :: removing repeated reports stops one event counting several times; pairs with :: CK-02 :: a model versus human agreement protocol measures extraction quality; pairs with :: IS-01 :: actors named differently across reports need resolving
typical_model_failure: Follows an event codebook poorly when run zero-shot and counts one event once per outlet.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; decision-informing:gold standard agreement; decision-informing:source-span citation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:gold standard agreement; high-stakes:source-span citation; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:provenance log; high-stakes:prompt variation
error_sources: input data; data transformation; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the schema is not fixed in advance (risk of bias), when zero-shot accuracy has not been measured (indirectness), or when duplicate reports inflate counts (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a table of events or relations, one row per extracted item, giving the actor, the action, the object and the time. It also gives counts by type and actor, and a sample of rows checked against the source sentence.

technique: Schema-based structured extraction with an LLM (LLM (large language model) information extraction; form filling from documents)
what_it_does: Fills a fixed set of fields, such as amount, date, party, stated risk or decision, for each document. Artefact: one record per document. Read the missing and "not stated" rates and compare a sample with the source.
fit_test: Fields must be explicit in the text, and inferred fields should be flagged. Validate each task against human labels. No error rates for extraction from filings were found.
status_and_evidence: Tested. GPT-4 performance across 27 annotation tasks and 11 datasets depended heavily on dataset and task (2023, abstract). ([Pangakis et al., arXiv 2306.00176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00176); [Halterman and Keith, arXiv 2407.10747](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10747v2))
purpose: Fill a fixed set of fields, such as amount, date, party, stated risk or decision, for each document, giving one record per document and the share of missing or not stated values.
use_when: Use when you need the same facts pulled from many reports or filings into one table.
requires_minimum: A fixed set of fields, defined before extraction, that are stated explicitly in the text.
not_for_text: Fields are not explicit in the text and the model must infer them without those values being flagged as inferred.
related_techniques: pairs with :: CK-04 :: a gold-standard sample measures field accuracy for each task; pairs with :: CK-17 :: a source-span check by code confirms that each value appears in the source
typical_model_failure: Invents a value for a field that the document does not state instead of returning not stated.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; decision-informing:source-span citation; decision-informing:prompt variation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:source-span citation; high-stakes:prompt variation; high-stakes:gold standard agreement; high-stakes:provenance log; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; data transformation; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when accuracy was not measured for the task (indirectness), when fields are inferred (risk of bias), or when not stated rates are high (imprecision).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is one record per document with the same fixed fields in every record, such as amount, date, party, stated risk or decision. It reports the missing and not stated rate for each field and a sample of records compared with the source text.

technique: Knowledge graph construction from text (entity-relation graph; ontology population)
what_it_does: Converts extracted entities and relations into a graph of typed nodes and edges, each linked to its source sentence. Artefact: a graph with provenance. Read paths between entities and areas with few or contradictory edges.
fit_test: Needs a fixed ontology and kept provenance. Extraction errors compound, and duplicates of one entity stay as separate nodes. No human-agreement figures for graph quality from text were found.
status_and_evidence: Documented. The survey abstract covers creation, enrichment, quality assessment, refinement and publication, and does not mention extraction from text. ([Hogan et al., Knowledge graphs, arXiv 2003.02320](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.02320))
purpose: Convert resolved entities and extracted relations into a graph of typed nodes and edges, each linked to its source sentence, giving a graph with provenance as a draft result.
use_when: Use when you need to trace paths between people, organisations or concepts reported across many documents.
requires_minimum: A fixed ontology and a source sentence kept for every node and edge.
not_for_text: No ontology is fixed and provenance is not kept, so extraction errors cannot be traced to the sentence.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-09 :: relation and event extraction supplies the edges; should follow :: IS-01 :: entity resolution stops one entity becoming several nodes; pairs with :: DM-21 :: social network analysis measures the structure of the graph
typical_model_failure: Keeps duplicate nodes for one entity and drops the link from an edge to its source sentence.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:human review sample; decision-informing:source-span citation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:source-span citation; high-stakes:gold standard agreement; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:provenance log
error_sources: input data; data transformation; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty drops because extraction errors compound across steps (risk of bias), duplicate nodes remain (inconsistency), and no agreement figures exist for graph quality from text (indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a graph of typed nodes and edges, with each edge linked to the source sentence it came from. It names the paths between entities and the areas with few or contradictory edges.

technique: Model summarisation of documents (abstractive summarisation; multi-document summarisation)
what_it_does: Writes a condensed text that paraphrases the content of one or many documents. Artefact: a summary. Read it only beside a check of each statement against the source.
fit_test: Use for orientation, not as a finding. No verified measure for current models on multi-document corpora was found.
status_and_evidence: Tested. Human evaluation found substantial hallucinated content in all neural summarisation systems tested (2020). Models use information in the middle of long inputs less reliably (2023). ([Maynez et al. 2020, ACL](https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.173/); [Liu et al. 2023, Lost in the middle](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172))
purpose: Write a condensed text that paraphrases the content of one or many documents, giving a summary as a draft result.
use_when: Use when you need a quick orientation to a set of documents before deciding how to analyse them.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The summary is used as a finding, or statements in it are not checked against the source.
related_techniques: pairs with :: CK-17 :: a source-span check by code catches summary statements that no passage supports; pairs with :: CK-19 :: atomic claim decomposition scores each summary statement against the source
typical_model_failure: Adds statements that the documents do not contain and under-uses information in the middle of long inputs.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:source-span citation; decision-informing:human review sample; decision-informing:prompt variation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:source-span citation; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:prompt variation; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:provenance log
error_sources: input data; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty is low because all neural summarisers tested produced hallucinated content (risk of bias) and long inputs are used unevenly (inconsistency).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a condensed text that paraphrases the content of the documents. It must be accompanied by a check of each statement in the summary against the source, and it is presented as orientation and not as a finding.

technique: Retrieval-augmented analysis (RAG (retrieval-augmented generation); grounded question answering over a corpus)
what_it_does: Retrieves passages relevant to a question and has a model answer from them, with citations. Artefact: an answer with quoted passages and references. Read the passages first and verify each cited claim.
fit_test: Fits questions that a few passages answer. Retrieval gives examples, not prevalence.
status_and_evidence: Tested. In generative search engines only 51.5 per cent of sentences were fully supported by their citations and 74.5 per cent of citations supported their sentence (2023). The original retrieval-augmented generator paper calls provenance for outputs an open problem. ([Liu et al. 2023, verifiability in generative search engines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.09848); [Lewis et al. 2020, arXiv 2005.11401](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401))
purpose: Retrieve passages relevant to a question and have a model answer from them with citations, giving an answer with quoted passages and a claims register.
use_when: Use when you have a question that a few passages in a large corpus can answer and you need cited support.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: The question asks for prevalence or counts across the corpus, since retrieval returns examples and not frequencies.
consumes: charter or question:agreed; raw dataset or corpus:raw
related_techniques: pairs with :: CK-21 :: reference-free grounding metrics score retrieval and faithfulness; pairs with :: CK-17 :: a source-span check by code confirms each quoted passage exists
typical_model_failure: Attaches citations that do not support the sentence they follow, and treats retrieved examples as typical of the corpus.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:source-span citation; decision-informing:human review sample; decision-informing:prompt variation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:source-span citation; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:prompt variation; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:provenance log
error_sources: input data; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty drops because sentences are often not fully supported by their citations (risk of bias) and retrieval may miss relevant passages (reporting bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is an answer to the question made of cited claims, each with its quoted passage and reference. It lists the retrieved passages first and marks each cited claim as verified or not against its passage.

technique: Exploratory data analysis with plots and distribution checks (EDA (exploratory data analysis); summary statistics; Q-Q plot; scatterplot matrix)
what_it_does: Examines a cleaned table with plots and summaries to find shape, outliers, trends, subgroup differences and violated assumptions before modelling. Artefact: plots (histogram, box plot, scatterplot matrix, run sequence plot) and summary statistics. Read for structure that summaries hide.
fit_test: Use before modelling. Treat findings as hypotheses, because reporting the most striking exploratory finding as a test result is the misuse. Plots of very large tables overplot and need aggregation.
status_and_evidence: Documented. Anscombe's four datasets share a mean, variance, correlation of 0.816 and fitted line, yet differ when plotted. The chapter contents from the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) list the plots and tests. Chart generation was the lowest-scoring category in TableBench (GPT-4-Turbo 62.00 against 86.3 for humans). ([NIST EDA chapter contents](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/eda_d.htm); [Wikipedia: Anscombe's quartet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anscombe%27s_quartet); [TableBench, arXiv 2408.09174](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.09174v2))

requires_minimum: at least one variable and enough records to show a distribution, usually 30 or more
not_for_text: Wrong choice when the most striking exploratory finding is going to be reported as a tested result. Very large tables overplot and need aggregation before plotting.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-04 :: profiling and rule checks give the quality findings that plots then explore; pairs with :: MM-02 :: plots show outliers and the algorithm scores each record; pairs with :: CK-13 :: findings from many exploratory comparisons need multiple-testing correction before they are treated as tests; substitutes for :: HE1-21 :: when the material is record-level tabular data and a full set of plots is wanted beyond distribution and base-rate checks
typical_model_failure: Describes plots it did not generate, computes summary statistics by mental arithmetic, or invents an explanation for noise.

It ends with a list of the shapes, outliers, trends, subgroup differences and violated assumptions found, each stated as a hypothesis.

technique: Algorithmic outlier and anomaly detection (Isolation Forest; Local Outlier Factor; Elliptic Envelope; One-Class SVM (support vector machine))
what_it_does: Scores records by how far they differ from the rest, using distance, density, isolation or a covariance estimate that resists outliers. Artefact: an outlier label or score per record. Read the top-scored records and decide whether they are errors, rare valid cases or a separate group.
fit_test: Choose by data shape: Elliptic Envelope for roughly Gaussian low-dimensional data, Isolation Forest for high-dimensional data with few assumptions, Local Outlier Factor when density varies. Misfit: flagged points form a dense cluster. Deleting flagged points without checking them is the common misuse.
status_and_evidence: Documented. One-Class SVM is sensitive to outliers in the training data. ([scikit-learn outlier detection](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/outlier_detection.html))
purpose: Score each record by how far it differs from the rest, using distance, density, isolation or a covariance estimate that resists outliers, and produce an outlier score and label per record.
use_when: Use when you suspect errors, rare cases or hidden subgroups among many records and want them ranked for review.
requires_minimum: at least 100 records and two or more numeric variables for the multivariate methods
not_for_text: Wrong choice when the flagged points form a dense cluster, which suggests a subgroup and not outliers. Deleting flagged points without checking them is the common misuse.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-04 :: rule-based checks remove impossible values so the algorithm scores real anomalies; pairs with :: MM-01 :: plots show whether flagged records are errors or a separate group
typical_model_failure: Names outliers by eye from a few rows, or picks a threshold to produce a desired count.

certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the choice of algorithm or threshold changes the flagged set (inconsistency) and when no flagged record is checked against the source (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is an outlier label or score for each record, with the top-scored records listed. Each of those records is given a decision: error, rare valid case or separate group.

technique: Clustering of records (k-means; hierarchical (agglomerative) clustering; DBSCAN (density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise); HDBSCAN (hierarchical DBSCAN))
what_it_does: Groups records by distance or density without predefined categories. Artefact: a cluster label per record, centroids or a dendrogram, and a noise label for density-based methods. Read cluster sizes, centroid profiles and stability across restarts.
fit_test: K-means assumes convex, similarly spread clusters and needs the number of clusters in advance. Ward linkage needs Euclidean distance. Density-based clustering needs a distance setting that is hard to choose. Misuse: treating clusters as natural categories when the algorithm always returns the requested number.
status_and_evidence: Documented. The documentation states that k-means inertia "assumes that clusters are convex and isotropic". ([scikit-learn clustering](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html))
purpose: Group records by distance or density without predefined categories and produce a cluster label per record, with centroids, a dendrogram or a noise label.
use_when: Use when you want to find natural groups among records and have no predefined segments.
requires_minimum: at least 50 records and two or more variables
not_for_text: Wrong choice when clusters are expected to be treated as natural categories, because k-means always returns the number of clusters requested. Misfit appears when clusters are not convex or have very different spread.
related_techniques: pairs with :: CK-09 :: validation indexes compare cluster numbers and algorithms; should follow :: MM-04 :: reducing many correlated fields can stabilise distance-based clusters; should follow :: PE-04 :: unit and range problems distort distances
typical_model_failure: Invents segment descriptions that the centroids do not support, or fits a pattern to noise.

error_sources: input data; data transformation; statistical assumptions
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when clusters change across restarts, algorithms or scaling choices (inconsistency) and when cluster labels are read as real categories (indirectness).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a cluster label for each record, a table of cluster sizes and centroids or a dendrogram, and a noise label where a density-based method was used. It reports the profile of each cluster and its stability across restarts.

technique: Dimensionality reduction (PCA (principal component analysis); factor analysis; non-negative matrix factorisation)
what_it_does: Replaces many correlated numeric fields with a few components that capture most of the variance. Artefact: loadings, explained variance ratio and scores per record. Read loadings to name components and explained variance to choose their number.
fit_test: Fits correlated fields with linear structure. PCA centres but does not scale, so large-variance fields dominate unless standardised. Misfit: the first components explain little variance, or loadings cannot be interpreted.
status_and_evidence: Documented. Non-negative matrix factorisation needs non-negative data. ([scikit-learn decomposition](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/decomposition.html))
purpose: Replace many correlated numeric fields with a few components and produce loadings, explained variance and a score per record.
use_when: Use when there are many correlated numeric variables and you want a smaller set of dimensions to read or model.
requires_minimum: at least 3 numeric variables and more records than variables
not_for_text: Wrong choice when the first components explain little variance or the loadings cannot be interpreted. Non-negative matrix factorisation also needs non-negative data.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-04 :: unit and scale problems distort the components; pairs with :: MM-03 :: components can be used as input to clustering of records
typical_model_failure: Invents plausible names for components without checking loadings.

error_sources: input data; data transformation; statistical assumptions
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when variables are not standardised (risk of bias), when components are named without reading loadings (indirectness) and when results change with the number of components kept (inconsistency).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a table of loadings for each component, the explained variance ratio for each component, and a score for each record. It names each component from its loadings and states how many components were kept and why.

technique: Survival and duration analysis (Kaplan-Meier estimator; Nelson-Aalen estimator; Cox proportional hazards; time-to-event analysis)
what_it_does: Estimates the time until an event while using records whose event has not yet been observed. Artefact: a survival curve with intervals and a median duration. Read curve separation and censoring counts.
fit_test: Needs durations with an event flag. Misfit: heavy censoring, or non-proportional hazards for Cox models (not confirmed).
status_and_evidence: Documented. The only source read is a software package page. It names the estimators and shows an event-observed flag, but it does not define censoring. ([lifelines on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/lifelines/0.23.1))
purpose: Estimate the time until an event while using records whose event has not yet been seen, and produce survival curves with intervals and a median duration.
use_when: Use when you need to know how long something lasts or how fast an event happens and some cases are still ongoing.
requires_minimum: at least 30 records with a start date, an end or last-seen date and an event flag
not_for_text: Wrong choice when there is no event flag or when most records are censored. Cox models also assume proportional hazards, which was not confirmed in the source.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-05 :: missing end dates must be separated from censored records; pairs with :: CK-13 :: comparing many subgroup curves needs multiple-testing correction
typical_model_failure: Ignores censoring and averages the observed durations.

certainty_limits: Certainty drops with heavy censoring or few events (imprecision), when censoring is related to the outcome (risk of bias) and when hazards are not proportional for Cox models (inconsistency).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a survival curve with intervals, a median duration, and the counts of records with an observed event and of censored records. It states whether the curves for the compared groups separate.

technique: Survey weighting and subgroup estimation (design weights; calibration; post-stratification; relative standard error)
what_it_does: Applies weights so that sample results represent the population, and reports estimates with sampling error by subgroup. Artefact: weighted estimates with standard errors. Read each estimate with its precision, and whether the subgroup count supports it.
fit_test: Use the weights supplied by the survey producer. Misfit: a relative standard error too high for the subgroup. Design questions need a person.
status_and_evidence: Tested. In an ABS evaluation, calibration with auxiliary information lowered relative standard errors by the order of 12.5 per cent and key-item non-response bias from 1.2 to 0.3 per cent. ([ABS Methodological News, Dec 2009](https://www.abs.gov.au/AUSSTATS/abs@.nsf/Lookup/1504.0Main+Features6Dec+2009))
purpose: Apply survey weights so that sample results represent the population and produce weighted estimates with standard errors by subgroup.
use_when: Use when you have survey microdata and need population figures, with precision, for the whole sample or for subgroups.
requires_minimum: the producer-supplied weights and design variables, and enough responses in each subgroup to give a usable relative standard error
not_for_text: Wrong choice when no weights or design information are supplied. A subgroup whose relative standard error is too high should not be reported. Design and calibration choices need a person.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-04 :: weights and codes must be present and valid; pairs with :: HE-05 :: the margin of error check tests whether a published precision figure suits the sampling method; pairs with :: CK-15 :: a representativeness audit shows where weighting must correct coverage
typical_model_failure: Ignores the weights and reports raw sample percentages as population figures.

tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a table of weighted estimates by subgroup, each with its standard error. It states the subgroup count behind each estimate and whether that count supports the estimate.

technique: Supervised classification and dictionary methods (text classification; fine-tuned classifier; lexicon method)
what_it_does: Assigns documents to predefined categories using human-labelled examples or word lists. Artefact: labels with confidence and a confusion matrix against human labels not used in training. Read precision (the share of assigned labels that are correct) and recall (the share of true cases found) for each category.
fit_test: Fits fixed, defined categories that humans can code reliably. Misfit: imbalanced or overlapping categories, or training data from another period or source. Dictionaries need explicit validation because word lists fail across domains.
status_and_evidence: Tested. Supervised learning outperformed dictionaries on a number of criteria (2021). Fine-tuning a natural language inference model on 500 texts matched classical models trained on about 5,000 (2024). Both are abstract-level findings. ([Barberá et al. 2021 via EconPapers](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:cup:polals:v:29:y:2021:i:1:p:19-42_2); [Laurer et al. 2024 via EconPapers](https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:cup:polals:v:32:y:2024:i:1:p:84-100_6); [Grimmer and Stewart 2013, Political Analysis](https://web.stanford.edu/~jgrimmer/tad2.pdf))
purpose: Assign documents to predefined categories using human-labelled examples or word lists and produce coded documents with confidence and a confusion matrix.
use_when: Use when you have fixed categories and labelled examples, or a validated word list, and need to label many documents.
requires_minimum: labelled examples for every category, usually several hundred in total, with enough examples of the rare categories
not_for_text: Wrong choice when categories overlap, are badly imbalanced or humans cannot code them reliably. Training data from another period or source also fails. Dictionaries need explicit validation in the domain.

typical_model_failure: Reports overall accuracy and does not show poor performance on rare categories.

tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a label and a confidence value for each document, and a confusion matrix against human labels that were not used in training. It reports precision and recall for each category.

technique: LLM coding and zero-shot classification of text (LLM annotation; LLM-assisted deductive coding; few-shot classification; natural language inference classification)
what_it_does: Applies a human-written codebook, or category descriptions, to text with a large language model (LLM). Artefact: codes, rationales and per-code agreement with human coders. Read the failing codes and the disagreement cases.
fit_test: Pilot on a human-coded sample, and require per-code agreement, repeated-run stability and error analysis before scaling. Misfit: agreement checked only overall, one prompt tried, or error patterns by group not examined.
status_and_evidence: Tested. Studies from 2023 to 2025 disagree by task. ChatGPT beat crowd workers on four of five tasks on 2,382 tweets. GPT-4 reached kappa of 0.79 or more on 3 of 9 codes and 0.6 or more on 8 of 9 in one case study. Across 13 million labels from 18 models, about 31 per cent of hypotheses reached incorrect conclusions. Errors on interview transcripts were not random with respect to subject characteristics. ([Gilardi et al., arXiv 2303.15056](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15056); [Dunivin, arXiv 2401.15170](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.15170); [Baumann et al. 2025, arXiv 2509.08825](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08825); [Ashwin et al., arXiv 2309.17147](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17147); [Ziems et al., arXiv 2305.03514](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.03514); [Pangakis et al., arXiv 2306.00176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00176); [Reiss, arXiv 2304.11085](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.11085); [Bano et al., arXiv 2306.13298](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13298); [Tai et al., DOAJ record](https://doaj.org/article/25c5015365a0467da462b8a73e3e2f56); [Törnberg, arXiv 2304.06588](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06588))

use_when: Use when you have a written codebook and a body of text too large to code by hand and want a model to apply the codes.
requires_minimum: a human-coded pilot sample with enough items per code to estimate agreement, usually 100 or more in total
not_for_text: Wrong choice when agreement is checked only overall, only one prompt is tried or error patterns by group are not examined. A rationale that sounds right is not evidence that the label is right.
related_techniques: should follow :: CK-04 :: a human-coded sample is needed for the pilot; pairs with :: CK-02 :: agreement against human coders and across runs; pairs with :: CK-10 :: repeated runs show stability; pairs with :: CK-12 :: a specification sweep shows whether conclusions depend on prompt and model; pairs with :: CK-06 :: bias correction is needed when labels are used in a numeric claim; substitutes for :: HE1-15 :: when a fixed codebook exists and the volume class is needs automation
typical_model_failure: Codes whole sets confidently without a validation sample, returns different labels on a rerun, and gives plausible rationales that do not justify the label.

technique: Sentiment analysis (polarity detection; opinion mining; affect lexicon)
what_it_does: Scores text as positive, negative or neutral, or by emotion. Artefact: scores per document and aggregates by group or period. Read the distribution and a sample of high and low scores.
fit_test: Fits when tone is the quantity of interest. Misfit: controlled language in policy documents and filings, or negation and sarcasm that reverse a score. Off-the-shelf lexicons need validation in the domain.
status_and_evidence: Documented. A text can be negative in wording and still support its target. ([Mohammad et al. 2016, arXiv 1605.01655](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.01655); [Grimmer and Stewart 2013, Political Analysis](https://web.stanford.edu/~jgrimmer/tad2.pdf))
purpose: Score text as positive, negative or neutral, or by emotion, and produce scores per document with aggregates by group or period.
use_when: Use when tone or emotion in text is itself the quantity you want to compare across groups or periods.
requires_minimum: enough documents per group or period to compare a distribution, usually 30 or more
not_for_rules: document_genre=legal or regulatory text|government or agency report :: controlled language in policy documents and filings gives uninformative tone scores
not_for_text: Wrong choice when negation or sarcasm reverses scores, or when tone is being read as position. Off-the-shelf word lists need validation in the domain.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-02 :: cleaning choices change scores; pairs with :: CK-08 :: validity checks test whether scores behave as tone; pairs with :: MM-10 :: tone is not stance, so stance detection answers the position question
typical_model_failure: Reports tone as if it were position.

error_sources: input data; data transformation; statistical assumptions
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when the lexicon or model was built for another domain (indirectness) and when scores are not checked against human ratings (risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a sentiment score for each document and aggregates by group or period. It shows the distribution of scores and a sample of high-scoring and low-scoring documents.

technique: Stance detection (position detection)
what_it_does: Labels whether an author favours, opposes or is neutral toward a named target. Artefact: a stance label per text and target. Read stance by source and over time, and the share of "none" labels.
fit_test: The target must be explicit and defined. Misfit: the target is not mentioned in the text, or reported speech is mistaken for the author's stance.
status_and_evidence: Tested. ChatGPT beat crowd workers on stance and three other tasks on 2,382 tweets, and GPT-4 was reported more accurate than experts and crowd workers on one election dataset. Both are single-dataset results, and the second page gave no figures. ([Gilardi et al., arXiv 2303.15056](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15056); [Törnberg, arXiv 2304.06588](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06588); [Mohammad et al. 2016, arXiv 1605.01655](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.01655))
purpose: Label whether each text favours, opposes or is neutral toward a named target and produce a stance label per text and target.
use_when: Use when you need to know who supports or opposes a named policy, person or proposal and how that changes by source or period.
requires_minimum: a defined target and enough texts that mention it, usually 100 or more
not_for_text: Wrong choice when the target is not mentioned in the text. Reported speech is easily mistaken for the author's own stance.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-08 :: entity tagging finds where the target is mentioned; pairs with :: CK-02 :: model labels need agreement checks against human coders; pairs with :: MM-09 :: tone and stance are different and should be kept apart
typical_model_failure: Attributes a quoted position to the quoting author.

output_spec: The result is a table with one row per text and target, giving the stance label of favour, oppose, neutral or none. It reports stance by source and over time, and the share of none labels.

technique: Framing analysis at scale (frame detection; issue framing; media frames coding)
what_it_does: Identifies which aspects of an issue a text emphasises, using a defined frame scheme. Artefact: frame labels and frame shares by source and period. Read changes in the dominant frame and the frames that are absent.
fit_test: Needs a defined frame set that coders agree on. Misfit: frames invented after reading, so the scheme fits the finding.
status_and_evidence: Tested. Frame detection was one of four tasks on which ChatGPT beat crowd workers in a 2,382-tweet study. The content of the Media Frames Corpus was not confirmed. ([Gilardi et al., arXiv 2303.15056](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15056))
purpose: Identify which aspects of an issue each text emphasises using a defined frame scheme and produce frame labels with frame shares by source and period.
use_when: Use when you want to know how different sources or periods present the same issue, using a set of frames agreed beforehand.
requires_minimum: a fixed frame scheme that human coders can apply with acceptable agreement
not_for_text: Wrong choice when the frames were invented after reading the texts, because the scheme then fits the finding. Assigning a frame to every document, including those with none, is a misuse.
related_techniques: pairs with :: CK-01 :: agreement statistics test whether coders apply the frame set the same way; substitutes for :: HE1-15 :: when a fixed frame scheme exists and the volume class is needs automation
typical_model_failure: Assigns a frame to every document, including those that have none.
minimum_checks: exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:gold standard agreement; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:gold standard agreement; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:independent review
error_sources: input data; coder or rater judgement; language model
certainty_limits: Certainty drops when coders disagree on frames (risk of bias), when the frame set was fitted to the texts (indirectness) and when some frames are rare (imprecision).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a frame label for each text and a table of frame shares by source and period. It names the changes in the dominant frame and the frames of the scheme that are absent.

technique: Probabilistic topic modelling (LDA (latent Dirichlet allocation); STM (structural topic model); mixed-membership model)
what_it_does: Models each document as a mixture of topics and each topic as a distribution over words. Artefact: topic word lists and document-topic proportions. Read top words, exemplar documents, and proportions over time or by source. The label is the analyst's interpretation.
fit_test: Fits long texts that contain several topics, when discovery and not fixed coding is wanted. Misfit: short texts, unstable runs, uninterpretable topics. Validation needs semantic, predictive and convergent evidence.
status_and_evidence: Tested. Models that score better on held-out likelihood "may infer less semantically meaningful topics" in large user studies (2009). LDA assumes each document is a mixture over a shared topic set, and STM adds document covariates such as time. ([Chang et al. 2009, NeurIPS](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2009/hash/f92586a25bb3145facd64ab20fd554ff-Abstract.html); [Blei et al. 2003, Latent Dirichlet allocation](https://jmlr.org/papers/v3/blei03a.html); [Roberts, Stewart and Tingley, structural topic models](https://bstewart.scholar.princeton.edu/publications/structural-topic-models-open-ended-survey-responses); [Grimmer and Stewart 2013, Political Analysis](https://web.stanford.edu/~jgrimmer/tad2.pdf))
purpose: Model each document as a mixture of topics and each topic as a distribution over words, and produce topic word lists and document-topic proportions.
use_when: Use when you have a large set of long texts and want to discover what they talk about, with no fixed categories.
requires_minimum: at least several hundred documents of reasonable length
not_for_text: Wrong choice for short texts, for runs that give different topics each time or for topics that cannot be interpreted. Topic labels are the analyst's interpretation and not a finding.
related_techniques: should follow :: PE-02 :: cleaning rules change topics, so sensitivity to them should be known; pairs with :: CK-08 :: semantic, predictive and convergent checks validate topics; substitutes for :: MM-13 :: when documents are long and multi-topic and the volume class is needs automation
typical_model_failure: Labels word lists with confident themes and overstates a theme found in few documents.
minimum_checks: exploratory:repeat runs; exploratory:spot check; decision-informing:repeat runs; decision-informing:spot check; decision-informing:sensitivity analysis; decision-informing:human review sample; high-stakes:repeat runs; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:sensitivity analysis; high-stakes:human review sample; high-stakes:second technique with different assumptions; high-stakes:expert review

technique: Embedding-based topic modelling (BERTopic; Top2Vec; clustering-based topic models)
what_it_does: Embeds documents with a neural model, clusters the embeddings and describes each cluster with distinctive words. Artefact: topics with representative words and documents, and an outlier group. Read the size of the outlier group and the exemplar documents.

status_and_evidence: Documented. The two papers report the authors' own benchmark claims. Automated coherence metrics were not validated against human judgement for neural topic models, and sometimes declared a winning model where human evaluation did not. ([BERTopic, arXiv 2203.05794](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.05794); [Top2Vec, arXiv 2008.09470](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.09470); [Hoyle et al. 2021, arXiv 2107.02173](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.02173))

technique: Word embeddings for concept measurement and semantic change (diachronic embeddings; concept direction)
what_it_does: Measures how terms relate in meaning within a corpus or across periods. Artefact: nearest neighbours, similarity to seed words and change scores. Read the neighbours before the scores.

status_and_evidence: Tested. Three embedding methods were tested against known historical shifts on six corpora, and less frequent and more polysemous words changed faster (2016, abstract). ([Hamilton et al. 2016, arXiv 1605.09096](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.09096))
purpose: Measure how terms relate in meaning within a corpus or across periods and produce nearest neighbours, similarity to seed words and change scores.
use_when: Use when you want to know whether the meaning or use of a term has shifted across periods or groups, or how close two concepts are in a corpus.
requires_minimum: enough text in each period or group to train stable vectors, usually millions of words
not_for_text: Wrong choice for small corpora, which give unstable vectors. Similarity scores are easy to over-read before the neighbours are read.

technique: Entity resolution and linking (record linkage; entity matching; entity linking; coreference resolution; blocking)
what_it_does: Decides which records or text mentions refer to the same entity by comparing attributes, with no shared identifier required. Steps: pre-processing, indexing (blocking), comparison, classification and evaluation. Artefact: match decisions or linked clusters. Read the match count, the uncertain pairs and the unresolved rate before counting actors.

Only a book description, a survey abstract and a textbook contents page were read. ([Christen, Data Matching, Springer book page](https://link.springer.com/book/9783642311635); [Papadakis et al., arXiv 1905.06167](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.06167); [Jurafsky and Martin, SLP3 contents](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/))

linkage: requires=no shared identifier; requires=shared identifier available
requires_minimum: records that share enough comparable attributes
not_for_text: Attributes are sparse, changing or unreliable. Blocking needs schema knowledge unless a schema-agnostic method is used, and no accuracy figures for matching without identifiers were found.

technique: Schema matching and ontology matching (schema mapping; field mapping)
what_it_does: Establishes which fields or concepts in different sources mean the same thing. Artefact: a mapping table. Read which fields are equivalent, partly equivalent or unmapped.

status_and_evidence: Documented. The tutorial gives a definition only. An annual evaluation campaign for ontology matching exists, but its page did not state the output format. ([Dong and Naumann, VLDB tutorial](https://lunadong.com/publication/fusion_vldbTutorial.pdf); [Ontology matching evaluation campaign page](https://oaei.ontologymatching.org/))

not_for_text: Fields have similar names but different meanings, or definitions are not documented.
related_techniques: pairs with :: IS-03 :: the mapping table is the basis for transforming sources into one model; should follow :: PE-04 :: profiling shows field types and values before mapping

output_spec: The result is a mapping table with one row per field or concept, giving the matching field in each source and whether the match is equivalent, partly equivalent or unmapped. It lists the unmapped fields.

technique: Common data model harmonisation (OMOP (Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership) common data model; data harmonisation)
what_it_does: Transforms source datasets into one shared structure and vocabulary so that the same analysis runs on each. Artefact: a standardised database. Read concept coverage, unmapped records (concept identifier 0) and capture differences between sources.

not_for_text: Many source values have no standard concept, or sources capture events differently. Only the OMOP instance was read; questionnaire harmonisation was not.

technique: Data fusion with conflict resolution (majority voting; deciding and mediating resolution functions)
what_it_does: Combines records on the same entity into one record and resolves conflicting values by a rule: choose an existing value (deciding) or compute a new one (mediating). Majority voting is the simplest rule. Artefact: a fused record per entity. Read which values were uncertain (a value against a null) or contradictory (different non-null values).
fit_test: Fits when entities are reliably identified. Misfit: mis-linked records or dependent sources. Voting suits only independent sources of similar accuracy. Text sources need claims extracted first, which adds uncertainty.
status_and_evidence: Documented. Truth changes over time, so the most common value can be out of date and the most recent can be wrong. Neither equal treatment of sources nor unchecked trust in accurate ones works. The strategy classification comes from a tutorial that draws on earlier work not opened. ([Dong and Naumann, VLDB tutorial](https://lunadong.com/publication/fusion_vldbTutorial.pdf); [Dong and Naumann, fusion strategies](https://scispace.com/pdf/data-fusion-resolving-data-conflicts-for-integration-45zt5kyc9h.pdf); [Li et al., A survey on truth discovery, arXiv 1505.02463](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1505.02463v2))
purpose: Combines records on the same entity into one record, resolving conflicting values by a rule, and produces a fused record per entity with uncertain and contradictory values marked.
use_when: Use when sources give different values for the same entity and you need one value with the conflicts shown.
requires_minimum: none
not_for_text: Records may be mis-linked or sources depend on each other. Majority voting suits only independent sources of similar accuracy, and text sources need claims extracted first.
related_techniques: should follow :: IS-01 :: entities must be resolved before values are fused; pairs with :: IS-06 :: copy detection stops voting from counting copies; substitutes for :: IS-05 :: when source_dependence is independent and sources have similar accuracy
typical_model_failure: Takes the most common value when sources copy each other, or the most recent value without checking it.
minimum_checks: exploratory:input validation; decision-informing:input validation; decision-informing:spot check; high-stakes:input validation; high-stakes:spot check; high-stakes:independent review; high-stakes:provenance log
error_sources: input data; data transformation; statistical assumptions
certainty_limits: Certainty drops with mis-linked entities, dependent sources and values that change over time (inconsistency and risk of bias).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is one fused record per entity, with the rule used for each field named as deciding or mediating. It marks each value as agreed, uncertain (a value against a null) or contradictory (different non-null values).

technique: Truth discovery with source reliability weighting (truth finding; source reliability estimation)
what_it_does: Jointly estimates the true value of each object and the reliability of each source from conflicting claims. Artefact: a truth per object and a weight per source. Read low-weight sources and low-confidence truths.
fit_test: Fits many objects claimed by many sources. Misfit: few claims per source, correlated sources, or objects with no conflict. Most methods start from uniform weights, which behaves like voting at first, and assume a source is equally reliable on every object. Evaluation needs ground truth, which is often absent.
status_and_evidence: Documented. The survey groups methods as iterative, optimisation-based and probabilistic graphical model, and does not rank them. A Deep Web study found surprising inconsistency across sources it considered relatively clean (abstract only). ([Li et al., A survey on truth discovery, arXiv 1505.02463](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1505.02463v2); [Li et al., Truth finding on the Deep Web, arXiv 1503.00303](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.00303))
purpose: Jointly estimates the true value of each object and the reliability of each source from conflicting claims and produces a truth per object and a weight per source.
use_when: Use when many sources make conflicting claims about many objects and you need to know which values to believe and which sources to trust.
requires_minimum: many objects, each claimed by several sources
not_for_rules: source_dependence=copied or derived :: correlated sources distort the reliability estimates
not_for_text: Few claims per source, or objects with no conflict. Most methods start from uniform weights, which behaves like voting at first and assumes equal reliability on every object. Evaluation needs ground truth, which is often absent.
related_techniques: should follow :: IS-06 :: dependence between sources must be checked first; substitutes for :: IS-04 :: when many claims per source allow reliability to be estimated
typical_model_failure: Reports source weights without a ground truth sample and treats agreement between copied sources as support.

tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result has a table of the estimated true value for each object with a confidence level, and a table of the reliability weight for each source. It names the low-weight sources and the low-confidence truths.

technique: Source dependence and copy detection (source independence analysis)
what_it_does: Estimates whether sources copy from each other, so that their agreement is not counted as independent support. Artefact: a dependence estimate for source pairs or groups. Read which sources should be grouped as one.
fit_test: Fits when copying leaves shared errors. Misfit: a source copies from a good source, so there are no shared mistakes to detect. Co-copying and chains are harder to detect.
status_and_evidence: Documented. In the tutorial example, two sources copy from a third, so treating them as independent would wrongly confirm everything the third provides. ([Dong and Naumann, VLDB tutorial](https://lunadong.com/publication/fusion_vldbTutorial.pdf); [Li et al., A survey on truth discovery, arXiv 1505.02463](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1505.02463v2))
purpose: Estimates whether sources copy from each other so that their agreement is not counted as independent support and produces a dependence estimate for source pairs or groups.
use_when: Use when several sources agree and you need to know whether they are independent or share one upstream origin.
requires_minimum: at least three sources with overlapping claims
not_for_text: A source copies from a good source, so no shared mistakes exist to detect. Co-copying and chains are harder to detect.
related_techniques: pairs with :: HE1-06 :: dependence results decide whether agreement counts as corroboration
typical_model_failure: Concludes sources are independent because the wording differs, without checking shared errors.

certainty_limits: Certainty drops when copying leaves no shared errors, and when sources are few (imprecision).
tag_basis: input profile inference; selection inference; sequencing inference; robustness inference
output_spec: The result is a dependence estimate for each pair or group of sources, stating how likely it is that one copies from the other. It ends with the sources that should be grouped and counted as one.

what_it_does: Takes qualitative and quantitative results on the same topic from a similar period, analyses each, then merges the results to compare them. Artefact: a comparison of results. Read agreement, partial agreement and discordance for each topic.

status_and_evidence: Documented. The source states that the extent to which mixed methods studies implement integration remains limited. ([Fetters, Curry and Creswell 2013, via core.ac.uk](https://core.ac.uk/download/127441332.pdf))

not_for_text: The strands measure different things, so discordance cannot be interpreted. Discordance needs follow-up: check for bias, assumptions, more data, re-analysis, theory or construct validity.
